The Spark.name: The Spark
The Spark.rule: An output becomes the next input
The Spark.tending: Each result feeds the next turn more, so whatever is growing grows faster and faster.
The Spark.fraying: Each result feeds the next turn less, so the growth slows and fades.

old_poles.tending: Compounding that builds
old_poles.fraying: Compounding that consumes

pole_cases.tether: Savings earning interest that piles up year after year.
pole_cases.snare: Debt where unpaid interest keeps adding to what is owed.

The Tide.name: The Tide
The Tide.tending: Each time it is pushed away, the pull back to its usual level comes faster and holds tighter.
The Tide.fraying: The pull back loosens, so each push carries it further off before it returns, or it stops returning.

old_poles.tending: Recovery a system genuinely needs
old_poles.fraying: The pull back to the setpoint resists a change that was needed: the same loop that gives stability is the source of resistance to change.

pole_cases.tether: A body's fever breaking quickly back to its usual warmth.
pole_cases.snare: A town snapping back to old ways after a needed change.

The Mark.name: The Mark
The Mark.tending: Each judgment leans harder on the old mark it is measured against, and the mark holds firmer the more it is used.
The Mark.fraying: Judgments lean less on the old mark, and it fades until it barely shapes what gets weighed.

old_poles.tending: Judging against a reference is what makes a judgment possible at all.
old_poles.fraying: Judging against a reference long after it stopped being true.

pole_cases.tether: A craftsman's trained eye catching every small slip in the work.
pole_cases.snare: An old salary figure making every new offer look low.

The Salve.name: The Salve
The Salve.rule: Reaching for what relieves the symptom
The Salve.tending: Each easing makes the next reach for relief come sooner and surer, so relief is sought more often and faster.
The Salve.fraying: The reach for relief comes slower and less often, and the symptom is left to sit longer before anything is done.

old_poles.tending: Reaching for relief now and then, where it can work, eases the symptom without stopping you from doing what you value.
old_poles.fraying: Reaching for relief by habit: each easing leaves the cause in place and dulls more than the symptom, so the relief is needed again and costs more each time.

pole_cases.tether: Pain medicine taken promptly after surgery so healing can begin.
pole_cases.snare: Drinking every night to blunt stress from a job never addressed.

The Nearest Light.name: The Nearest Light
The Nearest Light.tending: Whatever comes to mind first weighs more and more, and each quick judgment makes the next first thought arrive faster.
The Nearest Light.fraying: What comes to mind first weighs less, and judgments wait longer for what arrives later.

old_poles.tending: Judging by what arrives first, when what arrives first is the recent, current signal that matters most.
old_poles.fraying: Judging by what arrives first, when it arrives first because it is vivid, so ease of recall is taken for frequency.

pole_cases.tether: A driver braking at the first flash of red ahead.
pole_cases.snare: Fearing every flight after one vivid crash on the news.

The Keepsake.name: The Keepsake
The Keepsake.rule: Storing an episode by its peak and its close
The Keepsake.tending: Each time is kept more by its high point and its ending, and the rest fades from memory faster.
The Keepsake.fraying: The high point and ending hold less sway, so more of the whole time stays in memory as it was lived.

old_poles.tending: Storing each episode by its peak and its close compresses it into a story that can be kept and consulted: the remembering self 'composes stories and keeps them for future reference'.
old_poles.fraying: Storing an episode by its peak and its close until the remembered story overrules what was lived: a bad ending 'ruins' an experience that was mostly good.

pole_cases.tether: A hard birth remembered as joy because it ended well.
pole_cases.snare: A mostly happy trip remembered as awful after one sour ending.

The Easier Door.name: The Easier Door
The Easier Door.rule: Answering a simpler question than the one asked
The Easier Door.tending: A hard question gets swapped for an easier one more quickly and more often, and the easy answer feels surer.
The Easier Door.fraying: The swap happens less often, so more hard questions are met as asked, slowly and with less ease.

old_poles.tending: Hard questions get an adequate, if imperfect, answer instead of none.
old_poles.fraying: Confident answers to questions nobody posed

pole_cases.tether: A quick gut call when a choice must be made now.
pole_cases.snare: Judging a job applicant by how much they smile.

The Mask.name: The Mask
The Mask.tending: The story about who one is holds tighter against each new fact, and each fact pushed aside makes it surer.
The Mask.fraying: The story about who one is loosens as facts pile up, and each crack lets more of what is seen slip in.

old_poles.tending: Conviction that enables commitment
old_poles.fraying: A self you can no longer see around

pole_cases.tether: Staying a committed parent through months of feeling unsure inside.
pole_cases.snare: A gambler still sure he is lucky after years of losses.

The Mirror.name: The Mirror
The Mirror.rule: Taking form from who is present
The Mirror.tending: The self takes its shape more fully and faster from whoever is present, matching each new person more closely.
The Mirror.fraying: The self takes less of its shape from who is present, holding more of the same form across different people.

old_poles.tending: A self genuinely built by relationship
old_poles.fraying: No position independent of who is watching

pole_cases.tether: A new nurse picking up a mentor's calm bedside manner.
pole_cases.snare: A teen becoming whoever each friend group wants, losing any center.

The Namer.name: The Namer
The Namer.rule: Speaking as though words build what follows
The Namer.tending: Words spoken about what comes next build it faster and surer, each naming shaping more of what follows.
The Namer.fraying: Spoken words shape less of what follows, and what gets named drifts apart from what gets built.

old_poles.tending: Speaking something real into being.
old_poles.fraying: Speaking into being something that then works against you: saying 'I am sad', or 'I am bad', builds the self the words describe.

pole_cases.tether: Saying "we will finish this" and a team rallies to it.
pole_cases.snare: Repeating "I always fail" until each attempt bends toward failing.

The Riverbed.name: The Riverbed
The Riverbed.rule: Shaping conditions so one action is easiest
The Riverbed.tending: The setup makes one action easier and easier, so it happens more often with less thought.
The Riverbed.fraying: The setup steers less, so the action takes more effort and happens less often without thought.

old_poles.tending: Willpower removed from the equation
old_poles.fraying: Shaping conditions so one action is easiest works for whatever action the conditions are left shaped for: with cookies on the counter, you eat half a dozen without having thought of them, and no willpower is spent resisting either.

pole_cases.tether: Running shoes by the door make morning runs happen easily.
pole_cases.snare: Cookies left on the counter get eaten without a thought.

The Gardener.name: The Gardener
The Gardener.rule: Attending repeatedly to one thing among many
The Gardener.tending: Attention goes back to the same thing more often, and that thing grows larger and deeper with each visit.
The Gardener.fraying: Attention drifts to other things, and the one it used to visit grows slower and starts to fade.

old_poles.tending: What you attend to grows
old_poles.fraying: Attention paid to anger or fear waters those seeds too, and rehearsing them makes them stronger.

pole_cases.tether: Daily practice that turns a new skill into a craft.
pole_cases.snare: Replaying an old fight until the anger grows each night.

Escalation.name: Escalation
Escalation.tending: Each side aims higher faster, and every step up pushes the other's next aim further still.
Escalation.fraying: Each side aims a little less above the other, and the climb slows until the steps level off.
Escalation.push: Your own state is the other's reference: lowering it lowers their goal (Meadows' unilateral disarmament), or a negotiated outer balancing loop caps both. Neither follows from The Sliding Floor alone, whose push is to fix one's own reference.

old_poles.tending: Two people amplifying each other's best, both rising.
old_poles.fraying: An arms race neither chose and neither can exit.

pole_cases.tether: Two rival runners pushing each other to faster race times.
pole_cases.snare: Two neighbors building ever taller fences out of spite.

The Standoff.name: The Standoff
The Standoff.tending: Each pull meets a quicker, harder pull back, so the shared thing is held tighter near the middle and moves less.
The Standoff.fraying: Each pull meets a weaker, slower pull back, so the shared thing drifts further toward one side before it returns.
The Standoff.push: find a goal every party can pursue together, so the pulls stop cancelling.

old_poles.tending: Each party pulls the shared state back toward its own goal and each pull meets the other's counter-pull, so neither can drag the state far from where both can live with it.
old_poles.fraying: Each party pulls the shared state toward its own goal, and each pull draws a stronger counter-pull: rising effort from everyone, and no movement at all.

pole_cases.tether: Two co-parents keeping bedtime steady between strict and loose.
pole_cases.snare: A budget fight where rising effort from both sides moves nothing.

The Pairing.name: The Pairing
The Pairing.tending: The steady side answers each push harder and sooner, so the pair holds closer to one level.
The Pairing.fraying: The steady side answers each push more loosely, so the push runs further before it is pulled back, or keeps going.
The Pairing.push: Tune the brake to the drive instead of removing either: a brake strong enough to overcome the driver's reinforcing run grinds both to a halt, and one too weak lets the run away, so the steadier's job is to hold the driver near the limit, not to stop him. The Spark alone says output compounds and the Tide alone says a state returns to its setpoint; only the pair makes the balance between the two runs the thing to set.

old_poles.tending: The driver's run compounds and the steadier's run pulls it back toward a setpoint, each run taking the other's output as its input, so the pair holds a level neither would hold alone and can keep going (Meadows: 'neither loop dominates, and we have dynamic equilibrium'; Sellers: balancing loops that 'slow those who are getting too far ahead', 'to keep the game going').
old_poles.fraying: The balance tips: the brake overcomes the drive and the pair grinds to a halt ('the player will soon have insufficient resources to act'), or the drive outruns the brake and the run gets away ('the reinforcing loop dominated the system'); each then runs only as the other's opponent.

pole_cases.tether: A thermostat keeping a baby's room warm all night.
pole_cases.snare: A cautious partner pulling back every bold new plan instantly.

Watering Another.name: Watering Another
Watering Another.tending: Each notice makes the thing come up faster and more easily, until it grows on its own.
Watering Another.fraying: Notices come less often or land less, so the thing comes up more slowly and fades.
Watering Another.push: Water early and choose the seed first, because once a seed is strong it keeps growing without you ('If the seeds of happiness and love have become strong, they will manifest by themselves'), and a seed watered daily becomes 'much more difficult' to transform later, anger as surely as love. What knowing it changes is timing: the early waterings count most, and later ones cannot take them back. The Gardener alone says attend repeatedly; The Spark alone says output feeds input; only the pair says the choice of seed outweighs the amount of watering, because the watering stops mattering once the growth feeds itself. It differs from Flower Watering, where what comes up in the other answers to your words each time; here it outlasts them.

old_poles.tending: Attention starts a growth that then feeds itself: the capacity you watered keeps compounding in them after you look away.
old_poles.fraying: Water the wrong seed and it compounds just the same: each watering makes it arise more easily, until it comes up by itself.

pole_cases.tether: A teacher's notice helps a shy child speak up more.
pole_cases.snare: A parent's notice makes a child's whining come more often.

Answering For.name: Answering For
Answering For.tending: Each quick answer leaves the asker less able to work things out, so the asks come faster and lean harder.
Answering For.fraying: Answers come slower or less often, so the asker works more out alone and asks less each time.
Answering For.note: Helper and recipient each run the Salve: the recipient asks because an answer relieves his uncertainty, the helper answers because answering relieves the discomfort of not knowing; each relief is the other's next symptom.
Answering For.push: Change the helper's leg: both of you are reaching for relief. They ask because an answer relieves their uncertainty; you answer because 'giving it feels more comfortable than the ambiguity of asking a question'. Each relief is the other's next symptom, so the dependence grows from both sides at once ('The more you help your people, the more they seem to need your help'). The lever is your own discomfort, not their request: learn to hold the ambiguity of not answering, and count the cost of each answer in the reliance it trains ('you've trained your people to become excessively reliant on you'), not in the one exchange. Cutting help off without building their capacity only moves the dependence. The Salve alone says one stopgap atrophies the capacity it replaced. Only two interlocked runs say that the helper's relief and the recipient's relief feed each other, so the reliance cannot be fixed on the recipient's side. The helper, who can change only his own leg, has to stop reaching first. It differs from The Rescue, where each rescue confirms a story both parties keep; here no story is at stake, only two reliefs. It differs from The Shifted Burden (Salve + Tide), where the intervenor holds a setpoint for a system whose own balancing loop weakens and the lever is to rebuild that loop; here neither party has a setpoint, and the lever is the helper's own urge to relieve.

old_poles.tending: Expertise given generously where it is genuinely needed
old_poles.fraying: Expertise that prevents them developing their own

pole_cases.tether: A patient leaning on a doctor during a medical crisis.
pole_cases.snare: A parent doing every homework problem the child brings home.

Filling the Gap.name: Filling the Gap
Filling the Gap.tending: The early story holds tighter, and more of what the other does gets bent back to fit it.
Filling the Gap.fraying: The early story loosens, and what the other does bends less to fit, so the picture drifts.
Filling the Gap.push: Hold what you heard about the other before meeting as hypotheses, not conclusions, and test them against what you then perceive ('Assumptions blind, hypotheses guide'). The Mask alone says a story is defended against evidence; the Nearest Light alone says the first report wins. Only the pair says the first report becomes the story that is defended, so the fix is to keep what arrives first provisional until the meeting has tested it.

old_poles.tending: Assumption that lets you act without constant checking
old_poles.fraying: Assumptions made before meeting are kept against what one then perceives, so one deals with an unchanging, often flawed version of the other.

pole_cases.tether: Trusting a new surgeon on a colleague's word without rechecking.
pole_cases.snare: A teacher told a child is lazy missing every effort.

The Guard.name: The Guard
The Guard.tending: Each side answers in kind faster, so openings draw both in closer and walls push both apart more.
The Guard.fraying: Each side matches the other less, so an opening or a wall gets a weaker answer and the gap shifts slower.
The Guard.push: Set your guard by the relationship, not by the threat: lower your own armour to people who have earned the right to hear the story, and to them first, because armour held against everyone is what the other meets and answers with armour of their own. The Tide alone says return to a setpoint; The Mask alone says keep the story; only the pair says the setpoint must be tuned to who is across from you.

old_poles.tending: Each lowers the guard only as far as the other does: an opening met by an opening lets both come a step closer, and each one's measured disclosure is what the other meets and answers in kind, so trust is built between them while the story stays held back from anyone who has not met it ('Vulnerability is based on mutuality and requires boundaries and trust'; 'Being vulnerable and open is mutual and an integral part of the trust-building process').
old_poles.fraying: Each returns to armour whenever the other comes close, keeping the self-story safe, and each one's armour is what the other meets, so the protection prevents the connection it was protecting.

pole_cases.tether: Two new friends trading secrets and growing close within weeks.
pole_cases.snare: Partners matching each other's coldness until neither will speak first.

Reading the Room.name: Reading the Room
Reading the Room.tending: Each side catches the other's tension faster and closer, so the two moods hold more tightly matched.
Reading the Room.fraying: Each side catches less of the other's tension, so the two moods drift further apart before they line up again.
Reading the Room.push: Say your reading aloud as a tentative label and let the room correct it, instead of acting on it, because the first reaction you read is often your own (Voss: 'It seems like you worry that…'; Eijkelenboom: 'Don't assume you already know what the other person thinks'). The Nearest Light alone says you judge by what arrives first, The Mirror alone says you take form from who is present; only the pair says the first thing to arrive is your own mirrored state, so the check has to go back to them.

old_poles.tending: Emotion read as genuine, usable data
old_poles.fraying: Your own reaction mistaken for the room's state

pole_cases.tether: A nurse sensing a patient's fear before a word is spoken.
pole_cases.snare: A couple's small worry passing back and forth until both panic.

The Sliding Floor.name: The Sliding Floor
The Sliding Floor.tending: The bar tracks each last result more closely, so effort and results climb or sink faster as one.
The Sliding Floor.fraying: The bar follows the last result less, so effort and results move more slowly and steady out.
The Sliding Floor.push: Fix the reference: keep performance standards absolute, or anchor them to the best results (Meadows 241095). Knowing Mark and Tide separately does not show that the standard is itself moved by the performance it judges.

old_poles.tending: People take their standard from their recent results; while capacity genuinely grows, each gain raises the bar and they work harder to beat it: 'The better things get, the harder I'm going to work to make them even better' (Meadows 240626).
old_poles.fraying: The standard is taken from the last result instead of a fixed mark. Sliding down, each step is too small to notice, and 'everyone is lulled into lower and lower expectations, lower effort, lower performance'. Climbing, each gain resets the bar ('It takes bigger and better rewards just to trigger the same level of satisfaction and pleasure'), so no result is ever enough.

pole_cases.tether: A runner's rising times push training harder each season.
pole_cases.snare: A team's slipping scores quietly lower what anyone expects next.

The Shared Story.name: The Shared Story
The Shared Story.tending: Each telling fills more gaps from the other's memory, so the two stories blend tighter into one.
The Shared Story.fraying: They talk it over less, and each one's memory drifts back toward its own version.
The Shared Story.push: When two people agree about a shared event they have reminisced about together, count the agreement as one memory, not two: each fills the other's holes ('Your cousin is just as likely as you to misremember events from your childhood'), and 'Witnesses who exchange their experiences will tend to make similar errors in their testimony'. To use the second memory as a check, take each account before the two compare: 'When there are multiple witnesses to an event, they are not allowed to discuss it before giving their testimony.' The Keepsake alone says memory is stored by peak and close; only the pair says that the other rememberer is the correcting source that cannot correct, and stays a check only while kept apart. Transmission Drift carries one teller's retellings and the check against a recording.

old_poles.tending: Each recalls with the other's help, and each one's memory finds support in the other's, so the two keep a joint memory that binds them to something real.
old_poles.fraying: Reminiscing together, each fills the holes in memory from the other, so the shared account drifts from what happened.

pole_cases.tether: An old couple keeping a wedding day alive together.
pole_cases.snare: Two witnesses blending stories until a court hears one.

The Echo.name: The Echo
The Echo.tending: Each reading draws the part out more surely, and each part played makes the next reading firmer.
The Echo.fraying: The reading draws the part out less, and each part played proves the view more weakly.
The Echo.push: Change your own reading of the other against the evidence of their current stance (rule 13 practice on your own Mirror leg). Schelling: believing the dogs were gentle 'might have subverted the whole system'.

old_poles.tending: Two people genuinely shaped by each other
old_poles.fraying: Each takes the part the other's reading demands, and each part confirms the other's reading, until neither can be another.

pole_cases.tether: A coach treating a shy player as a leader, who becomes one.
pole_cases.snare: A child labeled the troublemaker acting worse with each scolding.

Gaming the Terms.name: Gaming the Terms
Gaming the Terms.tending: Each stricter line is met faster by a new way just past it, and each new way brings a stricter line sooner.
Gaming the Terms.fraying: New ways around the line come slower and rarer, and the line gets tightened less often.
Gaming the Terms.push: Tightening the threshold feeds the evasion. Read the evasion as feedback on the rule and revise it (Meadows 270679). Knowing Line and Outfall separately does not predict that enforcement deepens the distortion.

old_poles.tending: Creative compliance finding real slack in a bad agreement
old_poles.fraying: Letter satisfied, purpose hollowed

pole_cases.tether: Workers finding slack in a rigid contract to keep a plant running.
pole_cases.snare: Banks dodging each new capital rule with a fresh accounting trick.

The Naming Contest.name: The Naming Contest
The Naming Contest.tending: Each name is met faster with the other side's name, so the naming back and forth grows quicker and more insistent.
The Naming Contest.fraying: Each name is met more slowly or not at all, so the naming back and forth quiets and the words settle loosely.
The Naming Contest.push: When two of you have different names for the same thing, stop and agree one term aloud before going on, and do not take winning the name for settling the matter. The Namer alone says words build what follows; only the pair says two namings running side by side either converge on a shared vocabulary or turn the talk into a contest over the words.

old_poles.tending: A shared vocabulary built between two people
old_poles.fraying: Each names the matter in their own terms and answers the other's name with a counter-name, so the two duel over framings and naming replaces resolving.

pole_cases.tether: Two scientists sharpening a new term until both use it.
pole_cases.snare: A couple arguing over what to call the fight itself.

The Arrangement.name: The Arrangement
The Arrangement.tending: Each setup draws a counter-setup faster, so both sides build more and more around each other.
The Arrangement.fraying: Each setup draws less answer, so the building around each other slows and settles.
The Arrangement.push: When you find yourself arranging someone who is arranging you, say the choice outright instead of shaping another condition, because each arrangement you make becomes the condition they arrange around. The Riverbed alone says shape conditions so one action is easiest; only the pair says two shapers turn each other's arrangements into more to manage. Unsourced.

old_poles.tending: Each shapes the other's conditions so the right thing is the easy thing for both.
old_poles.fraying: Neither choosing directly, both managing the other

pole_cases.tether: Partners each rearranging chores so the work keeps getting easier.
pole_cases.snare: Office rivals stacking more and more rules to steer each other.

The Tested Price.name: The Tested Price
The Tested Price.tending: The first number named holds the deal tighter, and each later offer stays closer to it.
The Tested Price.fraying: The first number's hold loosens, so later offers drift further from it and are judged more on their own.
The Tested Price.push: When you do not know the market value, let the other side name first and prepare to withstand an extreme opening, then test any named number against an outside reference before accepting it. The Mark alone says a judgment follows its reference and the Namer alone that words build what follows; only the pair says the first number named becomes the reference, so the side with less information should not be the one to name it, and should not accept it untested.

old_poles.tending: Terms named and checked before agreement
old_poles.fraying: Terms named first and accepted untested: whoever names the first number sets the deal.

pole_cases.tether: A seller's opening price keeping a house sale on track.
pole_cases.snare: A lowball offer dragging a worker's pay down for years.

Held Silence.name: Held Silence
Held Silence.tending: Each quiet person makes the others wait longer, and the silence settles deeper the longer no one speaks.
Held Silence.fraying: Each quiet person holds the others back less, and the silence thins until someone speaks first.
Held Silence.push: Do not ask anyone to go first, and do not count on numbers alone: each keeps his view hidden for safety and each silence is the others' evidence, so even a majority that privately agrees stays quiet, 'nobody willing to be the first unless he has confidence that enough others will switch to make it worthwhile'. Take away the first move instead: arrange for everyone to show his view at once (a count taken together, a vote, an organised switch), so that no one's disclosure is exposed before the others'. As Schelling puts it, 'no individual will choose Right unless he expects others to do so; this condition will require some organized switch'. The Guard alone says to lower your own armour, and The Standoff alone says to find a goal every party can pursue together. Only the pair says why no one moves first. It differs from Critical Mass, whose lever is gathering enough people to pass the cross-over; here the people are often already there, hidden, and the barrier is the exposure of going first. It differs from The Hall of Mirrors, where members misread each other's views and information gathered before the reading is enough; here the views may be half-known, and what is missing is a way to move together.

old_poles.tending: Each keeps quiet because the others do, and by keeping the unspoken rule together they keep ordinary friction off the surface: on the train nobody talks to strangers, and the ride is easier for all (Lowery).
old_poles.fraying: Everyone privately knows; each keeps it hidden for safety and waits for someone else to go first, and each one's silence is the others' reason to stay silent, so no one is able to be first (Schelling; Brownstein).

pole_cases.tether: Strangers on a quiet train letting each other ride in peace.
pole_cases.snare: Coworkers who all see the fraud and none report it.

The Faithful Chain.name: The Faithful Chain
The Faithful Chain.tending: Each learner copies the teacher more closely and passes on more of the steps, even the ones no one can explain.
The Faithful Chain.fraying: Each learner copies less closely and passes fewer of the steps on, so the set changes or thins along the chain.
The Faithful Chain.push: Before a prestigious model demonstrates, strip the steps you know are irrelevant, because learners copy them anyway, and more so the higher the model's prestige (Henrich 274647). Where a step is causally opaque, do not prune it on your own theory. Borrowed Faith alone says the standard comes from the believed-in holder; The Contagion alone says form passes on without anyone deciding. Only the pair says that fidelity is set by prestige, so an irrelevant step spreads exactly as well as a working one.

old_poles.tending: Each learner takes a prestigious model as the standard, copies the whole procedure, including steps nobody understands, and later becomes the model the next learner copies. A craft passes intact across people who never met (Henrich; Connerton).
old_poles.fraying: Steps with no connection to the outcome are copied intact alongside the ones that work. The more prestigious the model, the more faithfully the irrelevant steps pass on, and no link in the chain can tell which steps are which.

pole_cases.tether: A village keeping a cooking step that, unknown to them, removes poison.
pole_cases.snare: Surgeons copying a mentor's useless ritual step for decades unquestioned.

First-Arriver Lock-In.name: First-Arriver Lock-In
First-Arriver Lock-In.tending: Each win pays out more to spend on the next round, so the leader pulls ahead faster and the gap widens quicker.
First-Arriver Lock-In.fraying: Each win pays out less toward the next round, so the lead grows slower and the trailing side can close in.
First-Arriver Lock-In.push: Pay the winner in rewards that do not bias the next round, or level the field periodically (Meadows' way out: handicaps, restarts, antitrust). The Mark alone says rivals are ranked against each other; the Spark alone says output feeds input. Only the pair says the ranking's prize is the next round's input, so the fix belongs on what the prize is made of, not on the judging.

old_poles.tending: The judges or market rank the rivals against one another each round, and the rivals reinvest the winner's prize as the means to compete again, so a real lead compounds and the contest resolves (Koster: 'not in itself a problem—it simply leads to victory'; Sellers: a divergence 'that can be useful').
old_poles.fraying: The first to get ahead, by whatever means ('bigger bribes, or whatever'), is paid in the means to stay ahead, so the lead compounds regardless of merit until the winner takes all and the losers are bankrupted or forced out; a novice arriving later cannot possibly succeed (Meadows; Koster).

pole_cases.tether: A clearly stronger team wrapping up the league title early.
pole_cases.snare: One early store buying out every rival in town.

The Hall of Mirrors.name: The Hall of Mirrors
The Hall of Mirrors.tending: Each hidden doubt makes the others hide theirs faster, so the group agrees more and more quickly.
The Hall of Mirrors.fraying: Doubts slip out more often, so going along spreads more slowly and the group agrees less quickly.
The Hall of Mirrors.push: Collect each member's private position in writing before anyone can read the room. Members 'can see others' behavior but not their thoughts', and once reading starts, early and assertive speakers set what every reader reads. Once the private positions are seen, the false consensus dissolves by itself: no coordinated move is needed, only the information, and it has to come before the reading and for the whole group at once (Kahneman: 'all members of the committee should be asked to write a very brief summary of their position'). The Echo alone says change your own reading of the other; Reading the Room has no push. It differs from Held Silence, where people keep quiet for safety and need a simultaneous switch; here they are simply wrong about each other.

old_poles.tending: Each member reads the room and the room is made of readers, so a group finds its mood fast and moves as one.
old_poles.fraying: Everyone reads everyone else's reading; private doubts never enter the room, and the group settles on a position no member privately holds.

pole_cases.tether: A team rallying fast behind one plan in a crisis.
pole_cases.snare: A board approving a plan that no member privately supports.

The Inner Circle.name: The Inner Circle
The Inner Circle.tending: More short words get made and shared, and newcomers must learn them faster to join in, or stay out.
The Inner Circle.fraying: The group's short words fade from use, so talk grows plainer and newcomers join with less to learn.
The Inner Circle.push: Define a term the first time someone new is present, because the newcomer will not ask (Hopson), and check that the listener shares a term before you rely on it (Lemarchand). The Naming Contest alone says members build a vocabulary, and The Frame alone says words shape the listener. Only the pair says that the vocabulary is also the entry test, so the terms that make the team fast are the same terms that keep people out.

old_poles.tending: Members coin shortcut terms and agree what they mean, and each newcomer learns to speak them, so the team's work runs fast in its own shorthand (Lemarchand; Schell).
old_poles.fraying: The same shorthand becomes the test of membership. Newcomers won't ask what a term means for fear of marking themselves as outsiders, members use it to show they belong, and people with useful ideas stay out of the conversation, until only the initiated can follow (Hopson; Lemarchand; Koster).

pole_cases.tether: A surgery team calling out quick terms mid-operation.
pole_cases.snare: A clique using slang to keep new hires out of meetings.

The Outfall.name: The Outfall
The Outfall.rule: Acting on your own account, and letting whatever does not appear on it fall where it falls
The Outfall.tending: More is done on one's own account alone, and more of what falls outside it lands on others unnoticed.
The Outfall.fraying: Less is done on one's own account alone, and more of what falls outside it gets counted and weighed.

old_poles.tending: The same non-billing lets benefits fall on others unasked: those who vaccinate their own children leave too few unprotected to sustain an epidemic.
old_poles.fraying: My exhaust falls on people who live by the road and never use it, and the town that throws its sewage into the river leaves it to the towns downstream: the cost lands on someone who runs no account against mine and cannot bill it back.

pole_cases.tether: Vaccinating one's own kids and shielding the whole town too.
pole_cases.snare: A factory dumping waste in a river that flows downstream.

The Line.name: The Line
The Line.rule: Treating a continuous quantity as pass or fail
The Line.tending: The amount is treated more strictly as pass or fail, so anything short of the mark counts as none at all.
The Line.fraying: The pass or fail grip loosens, so partial amounts count for more and a little bit becomes allowed again.

old_poles.tending: Deletes 'a little bit' as an available move, so restraint has somewhere to stand
old_poles.fraying: Deletes 'a little bit' as available credit, so partial progress reads as zero and people quit short of the mark

pole_cases.tether: A recovering drinker treating one drink as the same as ten.
pole_cases.snare: A runner quitting training after missing the goal pace by seconds.

The Learning Gradient.name: The Learning Gradient
The Learning Gradient.rule: Attending to a thing in proportion to how fast your understanding of it is still changing
The Learning Gradient.tending: Attention sticks more closely to what is still being learned, and leaves faster once a thing stops teaching.
The Learning Gradient.fraying: Attention sticks less closely to what is still being learned, and stays longer on things that stopped teaching.

old_poles.tending: Attention climbs with skill; you keep moving to the edge of your competence
old_poles.fraying: You abandon what still works because it stopped teaching you

pole_cases.tether: A student moving on to harder problems once basics click.
pole_cases.snare: Dropping a working craft the moment it stops feeling new.

The Cascade.name: The Cascade
The Cascade.tending: Each telling sparks more talk, so the scare grows faster and louder with every round.
The Cascade.fraying: Each telling sparks less talk, so the scare spreads more slowly and dies down.
The Cascade.note: poles first written in the registry pass; previously held only in conversation
The Cascade.push: When one risk suddenly fills every conversation, weigh it against the risks it is pushing out of view before moving resources, and treat the public fear as a harm to answer in its own right ('protect the public from fear, not only from real dangers'). The Nearest Light alone says the vivid case is judged likely; the Spark alone says output feeds input. Only the pair says the attention itself produces the next report, so the size of the response is set by the retelling, not by the risk.

old_poles.tending: A genuine risk gets the collective attention it warrants, fast
old_poles.fraying: A minor event inflated into panic that resets priorities while other risks fade

pole_cases.tether: Word of a tainted food spreading fast enough to stop sales.
pole_cases.snare: A rare shark sighting turning a whole coast into panic.

The Flywheel.name: The Flywheel
The Flywheel.tending: Each act makes the setting easier for the next one, so the act repeats faster and comes more easily.
The Flywheel.fraying: Each turn makes the act only a little easier, so it slows and takes more push to repeat.
The Flywheel.note: poles first written in the registry pass; previously held only in conversation
The Flywheel.push: Spend on the first small change of situation, not on willpower, and treat an early small advantage (or disadvantage) as bigger than it looks, because each turn of situation, thoughts and response multiplies it; if a nudge flops, try another. The Riverbed alone says shape conditions once; The Spark alone says output feeds input; only the pair says the shaping pays compound interest, so its timing matters more than its size.

old_poles.tending: The situation shapes the behaviour that improves the situation — your best self gets better
old_poles.fraying: The same flywheel turning on the wrong behaviour: each lapse leaves the runner in a situation that makes the next lapse easier.

pole_cases.tether: Running shoes by the door making the morning jog automatic.
pole_cases.snare: Phone by the bed making each night's scrolling start sooner.

The Agenda.name: The Agenda
The Agenda.tending: What gets named most seems to matter more each time, so it gets named more and crowds out the rest.
The Agenda.fraying: Naming sways what seems to matter less, so the most-named things lose their pull and the rest drift back.
The Agenda.note: poles first written in the registry pass; previously held only in conversation
The Agenda.push: Rank issues by a measure you choose, not by how often you hear them named, and if something must stay in shared attention, keep naming it, because what is named is what gets judged important (Kahneman: importance is assessed 'by the ease with which they are retrieved from memory', which is 'largely determined by the extent of coverage'). The Nearest Light alone says you judge by what arrives first, The Namer alone says words build what follows; only the pair says the namers set the ranking by setting the frequency.

old_poles.tending: Naming what matters keeps it in shared attention
old_poles.fraying: People rank what matters by how often it is named, and whatever nobody names slips out of their awareness.

pole_cases.tether: A charity keeping a forgotten illness in the public eye.
pole_cases.snare: News coverage making rare crimes seem like the biggest danger.

The Contagion.name: The Contagion
The Contagion.tending: Moods pass from one to the next faster and stronger, so each one met is caught more fully and carried farther.
The Contagion.fraying: Moods pass on slower and weaker, so each one fades sooner and reaches fewer people.
The Contagion.note: poles first written in the registry pass; previously held only in conversation
The Contagion.push: Go first, and count the reach: because a state one person shows is caught and passed on, whoever shows warmth or vulnerability first sets what the group spreads ('The snowball starts rolling when a leader is willing to be vulnerable'), and the effect reaches people the first person never meets, the recipient of a kindness 'being kinder to someone else down the line', so it is worth more than the single exchange suggests. The Mirror alone says you take form from who is present; only the pair says your form becomes the next person's presence. Each Other's Situation carries the standing conduct that shapes the people who share a setting; this figure carries the state that travels on past them.

old_poles.tending: Warmth, gratitude and calm caught from one person and passed to the next, without anyone deciding to pass them.
old_poles.fraying: Fear and anger snowballing between people; the pain of being avoided spreading

pole_cases.tether: Calm spreading through a room after one parent stays steady.
pole_cases.snare: Panic spreading through a crowd until everyone rushes the exits.

The Frame.name: The Frame
The Frame.tending: Each telling sets what the listener wants more firmly, and the listener takes up those words more quickly.
The Frame.fraying: Each telling sets what the listener wants less, and the listener holds the teller's words more loosely.
The Frame.note: poles first written in the registry pass; previously held only in conversation
The Frame.push: Before acting on a preference you formed from someone else's telling, restate the choice in the other frame (the loss as its keep equivalent) and keep only the preference that survives both. The Mirror alone says you take form from who is present; The Namer alone says words build what follows; only the pair says the words you take from others are where your preferences are set.

old_poles.tending: Another's words give shape to what you could not yet say
old_poles.fraying: Preferences frame-bound rather than reality-bound; narratives hijacked by whoever frames

pole_cases.tether: A friend's words helping someone finally name what they want.
pole_cases.snare: A seller's wording steering a buyer toward the pricier plan.

The Rising Peak.name: The Rising Peak
The Rising Peak.tending: Each fine ending makes the same choice surer, so it gets picked again more and more often.
The Rising Peak.fraying: The ending's pull on memory weakens, so the same choice gets picked less often.
The Rising Peak.note: poles first written in the registry pass; previously held only in conversation
The Rising Peak.push: When you decide whether to repeat something, put the choice in terms of the experience itself (how long, how bad, which part you would keep), not in terms of how it felt at the end, and when you design an episode you want repeated, end it well, because the memory that picks the repeat is set by the peak and the close (Kahneman: asked 'Would you prefer a 90-second immersion or only the first part of it?', subjects 'would certainly have selected the short option'). The Keepsake alone says the episode is stored by peak and end; only the pair says that stored episode selects the next one, so the error compounds into what you live.

old_poles.tending: Good episodes remembered well are the ones that get repeated
old_poles.fraying: You choose the repeat by its remembered peak and end, so you choose the worse episode on the strength of its ending.

pole_cases.tether: A family returning yearly to a camp that ends with fireworks.
pole_cases.snare: Repeating a dull job because its last day always feels warm.

Identity Ratchet.name: Identity Ratchet
Identity Ratchet.tending: Each act piles more proof onto the story of who someone is, so the story grows harder to change.
Identity Ratchet.fraying: Fewer acts add proof, so the story of who someone is loosens and becomes easier to change.
Identity Ratchet.push: Choose the identity first and cast small votes for it, and keep the identity small so that the ratchet that builds it does not lock it ('The more you let a single belief define you, the less capable you are of adapting'). The Mask alone says a self-story is defended; the Spark alone says output compounds. Only the pair says the evidence the story defends is made by acting it, so which story you start acting decides what gets built, and how much you stake on it decides whether it can be revised.

old_poles.tending: Acting the part manufactures the evidence that makes the self-story true
old_poles.fraying: The more deeply an action ties to identity, the harder it is to revise

pole_cases.tether: A new runner coming to see herself as an athlete.
pole_cases.snare: A man who calls himself a loner turning down every invite.

The Norm Cascade.name: The Norm Cascade
The Norm Cascade.tending: Each telling of the trend pulls in joiners faster, and each joiner makes the next telling surer.
The Norm Cascade.fraying: Each telling pulls in fewer joiners, and the saying comes about more slowly until it stalls.
The Norm Cascade.push: Never announce that a behaviour you want to stop is common, because the saying recruits it; name what people should do instead, and keep 'more and more' for the norms you want to spread. The Namer alone says words build what follows; The Spark alone says each output feeds the next; only the pair says a description of the crowd is itself a recruiter, whatever it describes. The Social Tipping Point's push (report direction, not level) is about timing a good norm, not about this.

old_poles.tending: Saying a trend aloud recruits the next adopter until the saying is true: 'Even just learning about an emerging norm can galvanize action'.
old_poles.fraying: Saying a trend aloud recruits the next adopter whatever the trend is: told that many visitors take the petrified wood, more visitors take it.

pole_cases.tether: Saying most guests reuse towels, and more guests start reusing.
pole_cases.snare: Saying many visitors steal petrified wood, and more visitors steal it.

Perverse Feedback.name: Perverse Feedback
Perverse Feedback.tending: Results swing back to usual faster after each high or low, and the judge more surely credits his last word for it.
Perverse Feedback.fraying: Results return to usual more slowly, so the judge links his last word to the next result less often.
Perverse Feedback.push: Before crediting praise or punishment with the result that follows, expect an extreme result to be followed by a more ordinary one anyway, and judge the intervention against people who got none (Kahneman: 'The control group is expected to improve by regression alone'). The Tide alone says performance returns toward its mean, The Nearest Light alone says you judge by what arrives first; only the pair says the judge reads the return as the effect of his own last act, so his feedback drifts toward punishing.

old_poles.tending: The judge answers each result as it arrives, and the performer's next result returns toward his usual level. Because the judge keeps reading the newest result, no single extreme holds his verdict: a bad attempt is soon followed by an ordinary one that he also sees, so his judgment of the performer moves back toward the performer's real level along with the results.
old_poles.fraying: Punishment looks effective and praise looks counterproductive, on a statistical artifact

pole_cases.tether: A shaky rookie bouncing back to form quickly after each poor game.
pole_cases.snare: A coach sure that yelling works, because rough days pass anyway.

The Anchor.name: The Anchor
The Anchor.tending: The first number holds the guess more tightly, so each guess lands closer to it.
The Anchor.fraying: The first number's hold loosens, so guesses drift further from it.
The Anchor.push: Assume the first number you have seen is pulling your estimate whether or not it carries information, and before committing, search deliberately for reasons the answer is far from it (think the opposite). The Mark alone says you judge against a reference; The Nearest Light alone says what arrives first dominates; only the pair says the first arrival becomes the reference, so the defence is to argue against it, not just to ignore it.

old_poles.tending: Starting from a first number, the judge makes an impossible judgment tractable, adjusting from it toward an estimate.
old_poles.fraying: The judge lets a random reference govern the estimate after it is known to be uninformative.

pole_cases.tether: Estimating a stranger's height from a known doorframe beside them.
pole_cases.snare: A randomly spun number pulling a judge's sentence longer.

Borrowed Faith.name: Borrowed Faith
Borrowed Faith.tending: The stated belief sinks in deeper each time, so the other side acts on it more and makes it its own faster.
Borrowed Faith.fraying: The stated belief sinks in less, so the other side acts on it less and it stays borrowed longer.
Borrowed Faith.push: Tell the learner, over and over, that you believe they can meet the standard, and watch what you expect of those you doubt, because an unearned expectation installs as readily as an earned one (Duckworth: 'a mentor who assures you, over and over, in word and in deed'; Rosenthal's 'bloomers' were chosen 'completely at random'). The Mark alone says judgment runs against a reference, The Mirror alone says you take form from who is present; only the pair says the reference they judge themselves by is your belief, so it goes where you go.

old_poles.tending: Someone they respect believes they can meet a standard, and that belief supplies a self they cannot yet generate.
old_poles.fraying: No standing once the holder leaves; low expectations install identically

pole_cases.tether: A coach's steady faith helps a player try harder shots.
pole_cases.snare: A manager's praise pushes a worker into burnout they won't admit.

The Presenting Problem.name: The Presenting Problem
The Presenting Problem.tending: Easy problems get brought and fixed faster, and each quick fix holds the talk tighter to easy ones.
The Presenting Problem.fraying: The hold on easy problems loosens, so the talk drifts more often toward harder problems before it is pulled back.
The Presenting Problem.push: When problems are offered, do not start with the first one mentioned or with the one you are surest of answering ('with the first challenge mentioned, or with the one for which you're most confident about providing the answer'). Keep asking 'And what else?' until the list is out, because 'the first answer someone gives you is almost never the only answer, and it's rarely the best answer'. The teller offers the familiar symptom and the helper picks the problem he can relieve, so each side's choice narrows the other's toward the easy problem. The Easier Door alone says a simpler question is answered; the Salve alone says relief is reached for; only the pair puts the substitution on both sides, so the fix is to widen what is offered before either side picks. Coaching the Ghost carries the case where the offered problem is someone who is not there.

old_poles.tending: The teller brings the problem nearest to hand and the helper, relieved to have an answer, answers it. Where the offered problem is the real one, the exchange is quick and serves both: when someone asks 'Do you know where the folder is?', 'tell him where the folder is'.
old_poles.fraying: Decent solutions to problems that don't matter; the real challenge never surfaces

pole_cases.tether: A help desk quickly fixing the password problem someone actually has.
pole_cases.snare: A patient mentioning a cough, never the lump that scares her.

The Rescue.name: The Rescue
The Rescue.tending: Each rescue comes quicker and proves the need more surely, so both sides lean on the pattern harder.
The Rescue.fraying: Rescues come slower and prove less, so both sides lean on the pattern less and it loosens.
The Rescue.push: Before you jump in, look at what the rescue pays each of you: the Rescuer gets to 'feel morally superior' and to believe 'you're indispensable'; the Victim has 'no responsibility for fixing anything' and attracts Rescuers. Each unasked-for rescue is evidence for both stories, so neither side will ask it to stop. Ask 'How can I help?', which forces the other 'to make a direct and clear request' and hands the choice of help back to them. The Mask alone says keep the story; The Salve alone says relieve the symptom; only the pair says the relief is what keeps both stories alive, so the check is on the story each rescue feeds, not on the comfort of helping (that is Answering For).

old_poles.tending: The rescuer genuinely carries someone through what they couldn't do alone.
old_poles.fraying: Each rescue is the evidence for the story that made it necessary

pole_cases.tether: A friend carrying someone through the first weeks after a loss.
pole_cases.snare: A parent paying an adult child's debts again and again.

Crowd-Out.name: Crowd-Out
Crowd-Out.tending: Each quick fix eases the pain faster and more fully, and the push to change the cause drops off sooner.
Crowd-Out.fraying: Each fix eases the pain less, so the push to change the cause lingers longer after the fix.
Crowd-Out.push: Count the pressure a placed fix spends as one of its costs, and never present the fix as the solution: relieving the harm also relieves the demand for the rule change, whoever offers it and however good the faith. Relief measures 'crowd out' support for 'more effective conventional system-changing policies', and the green-energy nudge 'gives people the false hope that the problem of climate change can be addressed without imposing costlier, but immeasurably more effective, policies'. The Salve alone says a stopgap atrophies the capacity it replaced; The Riverbed alone says shape conditions so one act is easiest. Only the pair says the capacity the placed fix spends is the pressure on the conditions themselves. The Two Hands (its child) adds that who offers the fix decides whether it complements or substitutes.

old_poles.tending: The fix people are handed can also crowd the rule change in: a personal step, once taken, carries its value forward into support for structural change ('They can crowd them in too').
old_poles.fraying: Once relieved, people stop pressing for the change that would have altered the conditions.

pole_cases.tether: Earplugs ending a needless feud over a neighbor's brief renovation.
pole_cases.snare: Bottled water handouts ending protests while the town pipes stay poisoned.

Choice Architecture.name: Choice Architecture
Choice Architecture.tending: The first or easiest option gets picked more surely, and the arranger keeps it in place more firmly each time.
Choice Architecture.fraying: The first or easiest option gets picked less often, and the arranger's setup holds more loosely and shifts.
Choice Architecture.push: Whoever designs the setting sets a default anyway, so set it to what the chooser would pick on reflection, and audit existing defaults for sludge (defaulting into unwanted products, auto-renewals). The Riverbed alone says the easiest action is taken; only the pair with the Nearest Light says the chooser also reads the option placed first as the normal one, so the designer's choice is carried as advice.

old_poles.tending: The good option becomes the obvious one, no willpower spent
old_poles.fraying: *Sludge* — the same machinery aimed against the chooser

pole_cases.tether: Water placed at eye level in a school lunch line.
pole_cases.snare: A cancel button buried so subscriptions quietly keep renewing.

The Focusing Illusion.name: The Focusing Illusion
The Focusing Illusion.tending: The thing in view swells faster and weighs more on the whole choice each time it is shown.
The Focusing Illusion.fraying: The thing in view swells less, so the whole choice is weighed by more than that one thing.
The Focusing Illusion.push: When weighing a purchase or a change of circumstance, ask how much of your future attention it will actually hold, and favour what will keep drawing attention (the weekly club) over what will stop being noticed (the new car). The Easier Door alone says a simpler question gets answered; The Gardener alone says attention grows what it touches; only the pair says the size of a thing in a whole-life judgment is set by attention now, not by attention over time.

old_poles.tending: Directing attention to what bears on the matter makes a global judgment possible
old_poles.fraying: Whatever is put in front of someone becomes the size of their whole life

pole_cases.tether: A doctor pointing at one test result to prompt quick treatment.
pole_cases.snare: An ad making one car feature seem worth a year's pay.

Each Other's Situation.name: Each Other's Situation
Each Other's Situation.tending: Each side copies the other's habits more closely, so the shared way of living spreads faster and sets deeper.
Each Other's Situation.fraying: Each side copies the other less, so their habits drift apart and the shared way thins out.
Each Other's Situation.push: To change what the people around you do, attend to the conduct they see from you every day, because that conduct is part of their situation: people who cultivate it 'influence others by shaping their shared situations', and the Confucian ethic 'sweats the small stuff', 'mannerisms, tone of voice, posture, and expressions' (Brownstein/Sarkissian). The same holds the other way, so choose your situation too: 'pick your peers', people 'who will keep you accountable, inspire you, and, most of all, enable you to do the same for them' (Duckworth). The Riverbed alone says shape conditions; The Mirror alone says you take form from who is present; only the pair says your own conduct is the condition, so no one needs to own the setting to change it. The Contagion carries a state passed on past the people you meet; this figure carries the standing conduct of the people who share a setting.

old_poles.tending: Each person's arranged choices make the good action easy for the next
old_poles.fraying: People hold each other to a bad norm; everyone waits for someone else to move.

pole_cases.tether: Roommates who both start cooking at home most nights.
pole_cases.snare: Coworkers all staying late because everyone else stays late.

Flower Watering.name: Flower Watering
Flower Watering.tending: What gets noticed and named grows faster in the other, and the other answers in kind more strongly.
Flower Watering.fraying: What gets noticed and named grows less in the other, and the answers in kind grow fainter.
Flower Watering.push: In each exchange, choose which of the other's seeds your words water, because what you attend to in them is what comes up in them then. Name concrete positive qualities ('see the positive qualities in the other person and express our appreciation for them') before raising a hurt, and notice when your words water envy or anger ('someone says something unkind that waters your seed of anger'). The Gardener alone grows what you attend to; the Mirror alone says the other takes form from you. Only the pair says that what you attend to in them is what comes up in them. It differs from Watering Another, whose lever is timing because the growth outlives the watering; here the lever is the present exchange, because the other answers to what you do now.

old_poles.tending: Attention to one real capacity makes it grow in someone who can't yet see it
old_poles.fraying: Unkind words water the other's seeds of anger and envy, and those are what come up.

pole_cases.tether: A mentor praising a quiet student's knack until it blossoms.
pole_cases.snare: Constant criticism growing more anger in a partner each week.

The Held Commitment.name: The Held Commitment
The Held Commitment.tending: The other side checks more often and more closely, so the promise is held tighter and slips back less.
The Held Commitment.fraying: The checking comes less often and less closely, so the promise drifts further before it is pulled back, or slips away.
The Held Commitment.push: Hand the declaration to someone who will hold the conditions, and add a pledge of your own at stake before that support ends, so the behaviour survives when the partner or the incentive goes: the group that took a self-funded commitment kept half its gain after the incentive stopped. The Namer alone says the declaration builds what follows; The Riverbed alone says shape the conditions; only the pair says the conditions are held by someone else, so plan for the day they let go.

old_poles.tending: The declaration stops being a wish because someone else holds the conditions
old_poles.fraying: The runner keeps the declared behaviour only while someone else holds the conditions, and reverts when the partner or the incentive goes.

pole_cases.tether: A workout partner who keeps a new runner showing up each morning.
pole_cases.snare: Constant check-ins holding a team to a plan already proven useless.

Dual Entitlement.name: Dual Entitlement
Dual Entitlement.tending: Each move off the usual terms meets quicker, firmer pushback, so the old terms hold tighter.
Dual Entitlement.fraying: Pushback against changed terms grows weaker and slower, so the terms drift further before anyone pulls them back.
Dual Entitlement.push: Before changing terms, ask whose reference the change moves: passing on a threatened loss is accepted, cutting the current holder's terms to raise profit is punished, and a newcomer holds no claim to the old reference (Kahneman: the firm 'is allowed to transfer the loss to others'; 'The replacement worker has no entitlement to the previous worker's reference wage'). The Mark alone says you judge against a reference; only the pair says each side's reference is the other's constraint, so the same change is fair or a violation depending on which reference it crosses.

old_poles.tending: Each side judges the other's terms against its own reference and punishes a breach of it, so an informal contract is enforced without a formal one.
old_poles.fraying: Both sides sincerely certain the other is cheating; any change reads as violation

pole_cases.tether: Neighbors keeping an unwritten fence-sharing deal for thirty years.
pole_cases.snare: A shop unable to raise prices even as costs climb.

Coaching the Ghost.name: Coaching the Ghost
Coaching the Ghost.tending: The pull back to the absent person grows stronger, so talk returns there faster and holds there tighter.
Coaching the Ghost.fraying: The pull back to the absent person loosens, so talk drifts more often toward the step of the one in the room.
Coaching the Ghost.push: When the talk turns to someone who is not there, pin the question to the person in front of you ('What's the real challenge here for you?'), because both of you prefer the absent party's problem and nothing in the conversation will signal the swap. The Easier Door alone says a simpler question gets answered; only the pair says the swap is mutual and satisfying, so it has to be broken by the question, not noticed.

old_poles.tending: Talking about someone who isn't there is how a hard situation first gets described at all.
old_poles.fraying: Both answer the easier question — what the absent party should do — and the person in the room, whose move it is, goes unexamined; the swap satisfies both, so nothing signals the error.

pole_cases.tether: Friends first sketching a hard family problem before anyone is ready.
pole_cases.snare: A couple venting about a boss while one's own choice goes unseen.

The Commemoration.name: The Commemoration
The Commemoration.tending: The yearly event is kept more firmly, so the shared past holds tighter and returns to mind each time.
The Commemoration.fraying: The event gets skipped or moved more often, so the shared past drifts and each one must recall it alone.
The Commemoration.push: To keep a shared past between you, put it on the calendar and do it together (the yearly visit), rather than trusting both of you to remember and retell it; the kept practice holds it where retelling would lapse (Connerton: the past is 'conveyed and sustained by ritual performances'). The Keepsake alone says each stores an episode by peak and close, The Riverbed alone says shape conditions; only the pair says the arranged occasion is where the keepsake is kept, so it survives either person's forgetting and outlives what it marked.

old_poles.tending: The two keep an occasion (the anniversary, the yearly visit), and by keeping it carry a shared past in body and calendar, not in either person's willingness to retell it.
old_poles.fraying: They go on keeping the occasion after what it marked is gone; their habit certifies a past that no contradicting fact can reach.

pole_cases.tether: Siblings keeping a late mother's birthday dinner every year.
pole_cases.snare: A couple keeping an anniversary trip long after the love ended.

Mutual Monitoring.name: Mutual Monitoring
Mutual Monitoring.tending: The pay keeps the watching steadier and sharper, so the free cover for others holds tighter where the watching pays.
Mutual Monitoring.fraying: The pay holds the watching less, so it slips and drifts, and the free cover for others thins out.
Mutual Monitoring.push: Let the monitor keep a private return for watching, and tie that return to the breach you need watched (the status of catching an infractor, a share of the fines, as the Spanish huerta guards keep a portion of the fines), because the watching lasts only while its private return covers its cost, and it follows only the breaches that pay: the Kirindi Oya secretaries pursued the taxes they were paid from and none of the 200 poaching reports. The Outfall alone predicts no one pays for a public good; the Gardener alone says repeated attention. Only the pair says the attention is paid for on the watcher's own account, so the design question is what the watcher gets, and for which breach.

old_poles.tending: Each watcher is repaid on his own account for watching (status and prestige for catching an infractor, a share of the fines, the sake collected from offenders), so he keeps watching, and the benefit of his watching falls on every other user unbilled.
old_poles.fraying: The watcher's attention follows what pays the watcher, and whatever does not appear on his account goes unwatched. At Kirindi Oya the administrative secretaries filed no actions against water poachers, though they 'regularly file cases in the event of non-payment of the acreage taxes upon which they depend for their remuneration'; 200 reports of poaching went unpursued.

pole_cases.tether: Fishermen policing their own waters and protecting everyone's catch.
pole_cases.snare: Officials chasing only fines that pay them, ignoring water theft.

Critical Mass.name: Critical Mass
Critical Mass.tending: Each person who joins pulls the next one in faster, and each who leaves pulls the next one out faster.
Critical Mass.fraying: Joining and leaving each sway others less, so the count changes more slowly in either direction.
Critical Mass.push: To start an activity that sustains itself only above a minimum, assemble in advance a group large enough to pass the cross-over and move them together; recruiting one by one below it just sees each newcomer drop out again. The Line alone says pass or fail; The Spark alone says output feeds input; only the pair says there is a count below which effort is wasted and above which it is unnecessary.

old_poles.tending: Past the cross-over the activity sustains itself and fills the room
old_poles.fraying: The same loop run downward empties it

pole_cases.tether: A new community garden filling up once enough neighbors show up.
pole_cases.snare: Rioting spreading as each new joiner makes the next more willing.

The Tradition of Non-Use.name: The Tradition of Non-Use
The Tradition of Non-Use.tending: Each side's holding back makes the other more likely to hold back, so the line holds deeper and surer.
The Tradition of Non-Use.fraying: Each holding back makes the other's next one less likely, so the restraint thins and either side may make the move.
The Tradition of Non-Use.push: Guard against the first use above all, however long the record: each side's restraint rests on the other's, so one violation lets the other follow at once, and the length of the silence is no measure of its strength (Tannenwald reporting Sagan: a tradition 'is easily disrupted by a violation, whereas a taboo is more robust'). The Line alone says a continuous quantity is treated as pass or fail; only the pair says each side's pass is conditioned on the other's, so a single fail resets both.

old_poles.tending: Each side's continued observance makes the other side's next observance likely.
old_poles.fraying: Brittle once broken — the other side follows suit

pole_cases.tether: Rival nations keeping nuclear weapons unused through every crisis.
pole_cases.snare: Two coworkers each staying silent about a problem nobody raises.

The Rising Sawtooth.name: The Rising Sawtooth
The Rising Sawtooth.tending: Each struggle or ease sizes the next step more closely, so the climb holds tighter to the learner's edge.
The Rising Sawtooth.fraying: The next step tracks the struggle less, so the climb drifts too steep or too flat before it corrects.
The Rising Sawtooth.push: Playtest with new players, not with yourself: the designer's own mastery sets the slope, and 'regular playtesting with new players' is what keeps the setups at the learner's edge. The Learning Gradient alone says attention follows the edge of understanding; the Riverbed alone says the designer shapes conditions. Only the pair says the shaper's own gradient has flattened, so the slope must be read off the learner.

old_poles.tending: The designer's arranged setups keep the learner at the edge of skill
old_poles.fraying: The designer's own mastery sets the slope, and the ramp outruns the learner

pole_cases.tether: A game that keeps each level just hard enough to learn.
pole_cases.snare: Lessons paced so closely the learner never meets a sudden leap.

The Mastery Problem.name: The Mastery Problem
The Mastery Problem.tending: The two stay closer in skill, so each one's push pulls the other harder and both learn faster.
The Mastery Problem.fraying: Their skills drift apart, so the push between them weakens and one or both learn less and drift off.
The Mastery Problem.push: When two players' skills diverge, change the contest (a handicap) rather than let them play straight, because the match teaches both only while both are still changing, and a straight match between unequal players ends the weaker one's learning at the first game. The Learning Gradient alone says attend where understanding still changes; only the pair says the opponent is the gradient, so its steepness has to be set on purpose. The Matched Edge's lever (who faces whom) is the next tier's.

old_poles.tending: A closely matched opponent is an endless source of new challenge
old_poles.fraying: When skills diverge, the weaker player stops learning and drops out: against a far stronger opponent 'you will quickly lose motivation because the match is too difficult'.

pole_cases.tether: Two chess friends sharpening each other over years of matches.
pole_cases.snare: Two rival nations matching every new weapon the other builds.

The Content Treadmill.name: The Content Treadmill
The Content Treadmill.tending: Each round of boredom sends the maker back faster, and new things come out on a tighter schedule.
The Content Treadmill.fraying: Boredom sends the maker back less surely, and new things come slower as the gaps drift wider.
The Content Treadmill.note: weakest Dyad confirmation: the Salve reading of the maker's move is interpretive
The Content Treadmill.push: Spend on the rules, not on more content: new content relieves boredom only until players' understanding stops changing, so add or change the underlying tokens and rules, or set up conditions that let players make their own paths (Sellers: new content that 'does not add to or change the underlying tokens and rules' bores; systemic design 'sets up the conditions that will guide the player in creating their own path'). The Salve alone says relief atrophies the fix, The Learning Gradient alone says attention follows what is still changing; only the pair says the makers' relief is outrun by the players' learning rate.

old_poles.tending: Each content drop relieves boredom and keeps production predictable
old_poles.fraying: Players learn faster than content can be made; the relief never touches the exhausted rules

pole_cases.tether: A weekly comic keeping loyal readers coming back each week.
pole_cases.snare: A small studio burning out chasing endless updates for bored players.

The Branded Line.name: The Branded Line
The Branded Line.tending: The talk about the named line grows louder and surer, so the line holds tighter while watch narrows to what the name covers.
The Branded Line.fraying: The talk about the line grows quieter, so the line holds less firmly and crossings face slower, weaker pushback.
The Branded Line.push: Name the outside of the line as well as the inside, and keep saying the line is absolute. A line held by its name holds only while its holders talk of it as unconditional, which is what frees it from depending on the other side's observance; and whatever the name does not cover, the same holders will let pass. So when you rely on a named line, audit what its name leaves out (the conventional destruction the nuclear taboo shields). The Line alone says pass or fail; the Namer alone says words build what follows. Only the pair says the line's strength and its blind side are both set by the naming, so the lever is the name, not the other side's restraint. The Firebreak (its child) concerns evaders gaming the line by degree; The Emerging Taboo the window before the name holds.

old_poles.tending: The holders talk of the line as absolute, and the talk is what holds it: a crossing by one party is not taken as leave for the others ('violation by one party does not necessarily constitute permission for violations by others'), so the line stands without waiting on the other side's observance.
old_poles.fraying: The holders judge every case by whether it falls under the name and let pass whatever falls outside it: attending to the named weapon, they leave weapons not so named free of opprobrium, so the destruction the line was meant to limit can be done by unnamed means (Tannenwald's 'permissive effect', defined 'in relation to the categories constituted by the norm or taboo').

pole_cases.tether: A ban on chemical weapons holding through decades of war.
pole_cases.snare: Managers who never fire anyone but quietly push staff out instead.

The Imagined Public.name: The Imagined Public
The Imagined Public.tending: The pictured crowd is built more and more from the nearest faces, so it looks more like its maker each time.
The Imagined Public.fraying: The pictured crowd draws less on the nearest faces, so it looks less like its maker and more varied.
The Imagined Public.push: Before you act on behalf of a public you will never meet, test your picture of it against people drawn from outside your own circle, because the public you imagine is built from the faces nearest you and agrees with you. Filling the Gap alone says check your assumption against the person in front of you; Reading the Room alone says your reaction is not the room's; only the pair says there is no one in front of you to check against, so the sample has to be sought.

old_poles.tending: You can act on behalf of a public you will never meet
old_poles.fraying: The public is assembled from the nearest faces, so each person's public looks like their own circle, and each is wrong in the direction of themselves.

pole_cases.tether: A local paper writing closely for its own small town.
pole_cases.snare: A politician sure the whole country agrees with their friends.

The Closed Circuit.name: The Closed Circuit
The Closed Circuit.tending: Each change comes back around bigger and faster, so both sides move further in the same direction.
The Closed Circuit.fraying: Each change comes back around smaller and slower, so both sides move less and settle.
The Closed Circuit.push: Act on whichever element you can reach, and do not wait for a first cause: 'There's no “first element” in any of this', so people coming out, public representation and attitudes each moved the others. Each Other's Situation alone says one party's arranged choice eases the next; The Flywheel alone says a situation shapes behaviour that improves the situation. Only the pair says every party's behaviour is also another's situation, so a change made anywhere counts.

old_poles.tending: Each party's change is the others' condition, so a gain made by anyone is fed forward
old_poles.fraying: The same coupling running downward: each party, held to worse conditions by the others, acts in ways that hold them there in turn ('Inferior jobs, inferior housing, inferior education which in turn again leads to inferior jobs').

pole_cases.tether: A town where new jobs bring schools that bring more jobs.
pole_cases.snare: Poor housing and poor schools keeping a neighborhood stuck sliding downward.

The Two Hands.name: The Two Hands
The Two Hands.tending: Each personal fix drains more of the push for change, so the rules tilt further and more fixes follow faster.
The Two Hands.fraying: Personal fixes ease less of the push, so pressure for a rule change builds and the rules tilt less.
The Two Hands.push: When the party the rule would bind promotes a personal fix, look for its other hand: find what it is lobbying against, back that rule change, and count the fix it offers as a substitute, not a first step (Chater & Loewenstein: 'point to the i-frame act on the s-frame'). Crowd-Out alone says relief spends the pressure for change whoever offers it; The Organized Few alone says concentrated interests shape rules the diffuse many do not resist; only the pair says the few spend the many's pressure with the relief so that their own rule-shaping goes unopposed, so the fix and the lobbying have to be read as one move.

old_poles.tending: The party that shapes the rules carries the personal fix together with the rule change, so the relief the fix brings adds to support for the rule instead of spending the pressure for it (health warnings that 'may serve to increase public support for s-frame measures'; s-frame policies 'reinforced with i-frame elements').
