old_poles.fraying: The concentrated few promote the personal fix to the many and lobby the rule with the other hand: the fix relieves the many's pressure for change, the few shape the rules unopposed, and the harm the rigged rules keep producing is answered with more personal fixes ('point to the i-frame act on the s-frame').

pole_cases.tether: Free helmets calming calls to ban a sport outright.
pole_cases.snare: Diet tips handed out while soda makers block a sugar tax.

The Peopled Street.name: The Peopled Street
The Peopled Street.tending: Each person's choice to go out or stay in sways the next person more, so the street fills or empties faster.
The Peopled Street.fraying: Each person's choice sways the next less, so the street fills or empties more slowly and unevenly.
The Peopled Street.push: Give people reasons to be out and places to sit and watch at every hour (mixed uses, walkable routes, porches), because each person out is the next one's reason to come out and the loop fails first at the hour when too few are out. The Arrangement alone shapes the conditions and Each Other's Situation alone says one choice eases the next; only the pair says the walkers are themselves the arranged condition, so the design target is the threshold number of people, not the street.

old_poles.tending: Each person out on a street with doors and windows is one more pair of eyes that makes the next person's walk safe.
old_poles.fraying: Each person who stays in because too few others are out makes the next person's walk less safe, and one by one the walkers stay home, though no one decided to empty the street.

pole_cases.tether: A busy evening street drawing more walkers and feeling safer.
pole_cases.snare: A scared block emptying faster as each neighbor stays home.

The Unseen Veto.name: The Unseen Veto
The Unseen Veto.tending: Dealings stay tighter on the people in front, and the ones not asked stay quieter, so asking them seems less needed.
The Unseen Veto.fraying: Dealings spread wider than the people in front, and the ones not asked speak up sooner, so more of them get asked.
The Unseen Veto.push: Before closing, ask your counterpart how the terms land with the people not at the table ('How does this affect the rest of your team?'), because the assumption that they speak for everyone is exactly what keeps the guarded party silent until it vetoes. Filling the Gap alone says test what you heard first against the person in front of you, and The Guard alone says lower your own armour; only the pair says the person to test the assumption against is not in front of you, so the question must go through the counterpart.

old_poles.tending: The negotiator takes the people at the table to speak for those behind it, and where they do, the party behind the table, whose interest the terms meet, keeps to its own position by carrying the agreement out; nobody has to check, and the deal is implemented.
old_poles.fraying: The negotiator keeps the story, built from the first people he heard, that they are the only decision makers, so nobody asks the party behind the table. That party guards its own story (status, self-esteem) outside the room, and its block arrives only when the deal falls through.

pole_cases.tether: Quick deals with a small shop whose owner speaks for all.
pole_cases.snare: A merger stalled late by a board nobody thought to consult.

The Authorized Version.name: The Authorized Version
The Authorized Version.tending: Each telling makes the agreed version stronger, so the story passes on more fixed and other versions fade faster.
The Authorized Version.fraying: Each telling holds the agreed version less tightly, so the story passes on looser and other tellings live on.
The Authorized Version.push: Read an authorized account as somebody's version: ask who agreed on it and look inside it for the dissent it still records, because tellers converging on one telling drop the versions that did not win. The Shared Story alone says two tellers' account drifts; Transmission Drift alone says a retold record ingrains its errors. Only the pair says the retelling settles on a consensus, so what goes missing is the dissent, not just the detail.

old_poles.tending: Older members retell a joint memory to younger ones, who retell it in turn, so knowledge is carried across generations
old_poles.fraying: The tellers converge on one telling, and the dissenter's version is not handed down

pole_cases.tether: A family recipe handed down unchanged across five generations.
pole_cases.snare: A town's story erasing the witnesses who remembered it differently.

The Organized Few.name: The Organized Few
The Organized Few.tending: The few shape each rule more easily, and each rule they win makes the next one easier still.
The Organized Few.fraying: The few shape each rule with more effort, as the many push back more and the next rule comes harder.
The Organized Few.push: Do not read the many's stillness as consent: it follows from each of them losing too little to act. Concentrate the diffuse side instead: organise the smallest coalition of the many that gains by acting on its own (Schelling: k, 'the minimum-sized coalition that makes sense all by itself'), or make the cost show on individual accounts. The Riverbed alone says the conditions are shaped for whoever shapes them; The Outfall alone says off-account costs fall on others. Only the pair says the shaped cost is spread thin enough to stay off every account, so the counter is to change the size of the account, not to appeal to the many.

old_poles.tending: The few shape the rules to their own benefit, and where their gain runs with the public's, the many, each acting on his own account, receive that benefit without paying for it: innovations that make money for their creators also serve everyone.
old_poles.fraying: The few shape the rules to their own benefit and spread the cost across the many. Each of the many loses too little on his own account to act, so the cost falls where it falls, and the few, unopposed, shape the next rule.

pole_cases.tether: Inventors shaping patent rules in ways that also spread new medicine.
pole_cases.snare: Sugar growers winning price rules that cost each shopper pennies yearly.

The Declared Interest.name: The Declared Interest
The Declared Interest.tending: Each named stake lowers trust in the advice, and the adviser leans harder, so trust falls faster.
The Declared Interest.fraying: Naming the stake moves trust less, and the adviser leans less, so the advice stays closer to what it was.
The Declared Interest.push: Do not treat disclosure as the fix. Remove the conflicted incentive, or keep responsibility for impartial advice on the adviser after he discloses, because the declaration is what moves the client's loss off his account. The Namer alone says words build what follows; The Outfall alone says what is off the account falls elsewhere. Only the pair says that naming the stake is what takes the client's loss off the adviser's account, so mandated disclosure raises the bias it announces.

old_poles.tending: The adviser names his stake before he advises, and the words do some of what they claim: the client's trust in that recommendation drops, so the adviser's own-account interest is weighed rather than hidden.
old_poles.fraying: Having named his conflict, the adviser counts the client as warned. He stops holding himself responsible for impartial advice, and because he expects his advice to be discounted he biases it further, so the loss falls on the client he warned.

pole_cases.tether: Buyers learning to doubt a broker who earns on each sale.
pole_cases.snare: A doctor who names drug-company pay, then pushes the drug harder.

The Tipped Hand.name: The Tipped Hand
The Tipped Hand.tending: Each voice of support comes faster and makes the next doubt harder to say, so the line forms tighter.
The Tipped Hand.fraying: Each voice of support makes the next doubt less hard to say, so the line forms looser and slower.
The Tipped Hand.push: Before the team commits and before the leader's preference is known, run a premortem: 'Imagine that we are a year into the future... The outcome was a disaster. Please take 5 to 10 minutes to write a brief history of that disaster.' Naming the disaster first makes doubt what spreads. The Agenda alone says naming keeps a thing in attention; The Norm Cascade alone says saying a trend recruits; only the pair says whichever is named first by the leader sets what the team will voice.

old_poles.tending: Once a course is named, each member voices commitment to it, setting aside private disagreement, and each one's commitment is what the next member sees and joins, so the team converges and carries the plan out together ('disagree and commit'; 'supporting it with your actions').
old_poles.fraying: Name the plan first and dissent reads as disloyalty

pole_cases.tether: A team rallying behind a chosen plan to ship on time.
pole_cases.snare: A board approving a doomed deal because no one dared object.

The Split Ledger.name: The Split Ledger
The Split Ledger.tending: Each side holds back help more quickly and more fully, and each holdback makes the other hold back harder.
The Split Ledger.fraying: Each side holds back less, so help flows more freely and the holding back spreads more slowly.
The Split Ledger.push: Pay on the unit that has to win: where the team must win together, use team incentives ('When you want to encourage teamwork, you need to use team incentives'), built to guard against free riding, because members follow the money and not the talking points. The Mark alone says a result is judged against a reference; The Outfall alone says off-account effects fall elsewhere. Only the pair says the reference is the teammate, so every unbilled harm to him counts as a gain, and the fix is to change whose result is on the account.

old_poles.tending: Each member judges his result against his teammates' and works on his own account to beat it, so everyone works harder, and where the team wins by its best member, the rivalry pushes the best one further.
old_poles.fraying: Each member judges his result against his teammates' and acts on his own account, so help that would raise a teammate's result is withheld and a teammate's work may even be sabotaged, because a rival's loss is his relative gain. The team result, on nobody's account, falls where it falls.

pole_cases.tether: Rival sprinters each training alone and pushing each other to records.
pole_cases.snare: A sales team hiding leads from each other while total sales drop.

Never Enough.name: Never Enough
Never Enough.tending: Each reached aim gets raised faster and higher, so the aim climbs more steeply from the lives in view.
Never Enough.fraying: Each reached aim gets raised less and slower, so the aim levels off and stays near reach longer.
Never Enough.push: Choose whom you compare against, not only how: a standard still slides if it is taken from the most visible lives, so compare against lives you can see whole and name what is enough before the next gain resets the floor (Brown: 'The opposite of scarcity is enough'). The Sliding Floor alone says fix the reference against its own drift, The Anchor alone says the first reference governs; only the pair says the reference is drawn from whoever is most visible, so fixing it is not enough without choosing it.

old_poles.tending: People take their reference from those they see and raise their standard as they reach it, so what they attempt keeps rising, and each can still reach a point they call enough.
old_poles.fraying: People take the most visible lives as their reference, and each resets the floor faster than anyone can reach it.

pole_cases.tether: An athlete raising targets each season and breaking records.
pole_cases.snare: A family upgrading houses again and again, never feeling settled.

The Standing Rite.name: The Standing Rite
The Standing Rite.tending: Each showing-up reminds the others more strongly, so more come each year and the shared past holds tighter.
The Standing Rite.fraying: Each showing-up reminds the others less, so fewer come and the shared past the event acts out loosens.
The Standing Rite.push: Whether a group shares a past depends on whether its members keep performing together on the dates, not on whether the past is true or retold ('commemorative ceremonies prove to be commemorative only in so far as they are performative'). So to keep a shared past, keep the joint performance going; to judge one, look at what the rite performs, because the participants will come to hold whatever it carries. The Shared Story alone says check memory against a recording; The Commemoration alone says the kept occasion carries the past; only the pair says the participants' joint memory lasts exactly as long as their joint performance, so it is kept or lost by acting on who performs together. It differs from The Enacted Telling, whose lever is the content of a narrative fused to a rite; here the lever is the performing group itself.

old_poles.tending: Participants who keep the scheduled bodily occasion hold a common past that no one has to argue for.
old_poles.fraying: Participants who keep the scheduled occasion together hold whatever past it performs, invented or not. Each one's performance is the others' reminder, so a newly invented calendar becomes the common past without anyone arguing for it: the subjects of the Third Reich 'were constantly reminded of the National Socialist Party and its ideology by a series of commemorative ceremonies', and 'the impact of this newly-invented canonic sequence pervaded all spheres of life'.

pole_cases.tether: A town's yearly memorial keeping the names of its fallen known.
pole_cases.snare: A regime's invented holidays binding people to a made-up history.

The Enacted Telling.name: The Enacted Telling
The Enacted Telling.tending: Each yearly telling fixes the drifted version tighter, so words against it reach it less and less.
The Enacted Telling.fraying: The yearly telling is kept more loosely, so words against the story start to reach it and the version shifts.
The Enacted Telling.push: To change what a community tells about its past, change what it does on its dates, because a correction in print leaves the re-enactment untouched; the actors in a new beginning register it 'by inaugurating a new calendar' (Connerton). Transmission Drift alone says a retold record drifts and is ingrained, and corrects it against a recording. The Commemoration alone says a kept occasion carries a past. Only the pair says the drifted telling is re-enacted on the occasion, so the correction has to enter the rite and a recording will not reach it. It differs from The Standing Rite, whose lever is who keeps performing together; here the lever is what the performance says.

old_poles.tending: A community retells its past fused to calendar, setting and body, and by re-enacting it carries an identity.
old_poles.fraying: Those who re-enact the telling on its dates hold its drifted version fixed. Each year they re-present a past 'transfigured by mythicisation into unchanging and unchangeable substances', whose contents 'are represented as being not subject to any kind of change'. A critic who argues against the story is arguing with something the participants do rather than something they claim, and it stands until they change the ceremony.

pole_cases.tether: A people keeping its language alive through festival songs.
pole_cases.snare: A town's parade keeping a made-up hero's story beyond question.

The Contingent Commitment.name: The Contingent Commitment
The Contingent Commitment.tending: Each seen keeping or slip spreads to the other faster, so both sides keep, or slip, more surely.
The Contingent Commitment.fraying: Each seen keeping or slip sways the other less, so what one does spreads more weakly to the other.
The Contingent Commitment.push: Keep the rules cheap to watch, so that each user's own watching tells him the compliance rate, and treat a fall in watching as a fall in compliance. The watcher is himself what the others watch, and his compliance runs on what he sees more than on any sanction ('Contingent self-commitments and mutual monitoring reinforce one another, especially when appropriators have devised rules that tend to reduce monitoring costs'). Mutual Monitoring alone says the monitor is paid privately in information. Only the pairing says that this information is what keeps the watcher's own compliance going. It differs from The Watched Promise, whose lever is the size of the sanction the watcher sets; here nothing is sanctioned, and the lever is the cost of watching.

old_poles.tending: Each appropriator watches the others while using his own turn, finds that they comply, and so keeps complying himself, and his compliance is what they see when they watch him. Contingent commitment and mutual watching keep each other going (Ostrom 287426).
old_poles.fraying: The same watch, once it keeps finding breakers, tells each watcher he may be the sucker, so he complies less, the next watcher finds more infractions, and 'rule compliance will cascade downward'. Compliers with 'a limited tolerance to the evidence or to the mere suspicion that others are cheating' drop out as the evidence arrives, and the homeowner who hears the sprinklers in the dark turns on his own (Schelling).

pole_cases.tether: Neighbors who each keep a water-sharing deal because others do.
pole_cases.snare: One seen cheater sending a whole group's rule-keeping sliding fast.

The Social Tipping Point.name: The Social Tipping Point
The Social Tipping Point.tending: Each person who joins gives the speakers more to point to, so the next person joins sooner and the flip nears faster.
The Social Tipping Point.fraying: Each joiner adds less to point to, so new people join slower and the count climbs more slowly toward the flip.
The Social Tipping Point.note: Kept on the parsimony test: Critical Mass has a threshold but no message; The Norm Cascade has a message but no threshold.
The Social Tipping Point.push: Before a norm is mainstream, report which way it is moving rather than how widespread it is, and do not read a lack of visible progress as distance from the threshold, because nobody can see where the threshold is.

old_poles.tending: Messengers who say 'more and more' carry a norm that has not yet gone mainstream through its slow phase. Each person they recruit moves the count toward a threshold nobody can see, and once past it the norm spreads suddenly.
old_poles.fraying: Because the threshold cannot be seen, every step toward it looks like a drop in the bucket, and people give up on work that may have been close. The same cascade can also run back out as fast as it came in: masks on, then masks off.

pole_cases.tether: Seatbelt use spreading as more drivers hear that others buckle up.
pole_cases.snare: A fad diet sweeping a town as each convert recruits the next.

The Matched Edge.name: The Matched Edge
The Matched Edge.tending: Each result steers the next pairing more tightly to the edge of what each player can do.
The Matched Edge.fraying: Each result steers the next pairing more loosely, so matches drift further from the edge of what players can do.
The Matched Edge.push: Keep opponent choice with the matchmaker and match on skill, because learners left to choose take the sure wins (Koster: bottom-feeding, 'a player will intentionally take on weaker opponents'; Hopson: 'Bungie would choose the map, gametype, and the opponents'). The Rising Sawtooth alone says the designer's own mastery sets the slope, The Mastery Problem alone says divergent skill eliminates beginners; only the pair says the designer's arranging has to be of the other learner, not the level.

old_poles.tending: The designer's matching and the learners' results run together: each match's result updates the ranking, and the ranking sets each learner's next opponent at the edge of his skill, so every match teaches both players and newcomers meet newcomers. Players who expected to hate giving up the choice got 'fair and accurate online matchmaking in a large online population', and 'Players loved the new system'.
old_poles.fraying: The matchmaker's own matching misses the edge: it pairs players who are not 'very precisely of their skill level', each lopsided result feeds the next pairing, the strong 'reinforce their position by repeatedly defeating easy targets', the novice 'cannot possibly succeed', and the losers quit.

pole_cases.tether: An online game matching beginners with beginners as they improve.
pole_cases.snare: Every match so close that players never get an easy win.

Players as Content.name: Players as Content
Players as Content.tending: Each new player freshens the game more, and the fresher game draws newcomers faster.
Players as Content.fraying: Each new player changes the game less, so newcomers arrive more slowly and play settles into the same few patterns.
Players as Content.push: When other players are the content, matchmaking is the content supply: match each newcomer 'very precisely' to skill and keep beginners out of veterans' reach, because every beginner eliminated in a first match is future content lost. The Mastery Problem alone says mismatched opponents drive the weaker out; the Content Treadmill alone says content runs out faster than it is made. Only the pair says the newcomers are the content, so protecting their inflow replaces the production budget.

old_poles.tending: Other learners become the content, and their still-changing play keeps challenge fresh
old_poles.fraying: The skill gap becomes a wall, newcomers stop arriving, and a game whose content is its players runs out of content as the veterans leave.

pole_cases.tether: A chess club whose new members keep every match surprising.
pole_cases.snare: A party game spreading so fast it swallows every evening.

The Emerging Taboo.name: The Emerging Taboo
The Emerging Taboo.tending: Each round of holding back makes the next one surer, until the act becomes unthinkable to both sides.
The Emerging Taboo.fraying: Holding back grows less sure each round, so each side waits more on the other and one break could end it.
The Emerging Taboo.push: If the restraint is broken while it is still emerging, how the other holders respond decides whether it breaks: treat the use as an aberration and answer it with new measures, so the violation strengthens the line instead of resetting it. The Tradition of Non-Use alone says observance breeds observance and is brittle once broken; The Branded Line alone says a name can hold a line; only the pair says the window's outcome is set by the response to the first break, not by the break.

old_poles.tending: Each year the holders observe the named restraint, they move it from prudence toward the unthinkable, until they no longer need the other side to observe it.
old_poles.fraying: In the window before they stop depending on the other side, the holders keep the restraint only as long as the others do, and a deliberate use by one of the few major holders is the case most likely to break the record and the name at once: 'The harder case would be deliberate, “rational” use by one of the major nuclear powers, such as the United States.'

pole_cases.tether: Nations never using nuclear weapons, year after year.
pole_cases.snare: Coworkers never asking about pay, until no one dares to ask.

The Inherited Ground.name: The Inherited Ground
The Inherited Ground.tending: Each new group of children takes on the adults' ways more fully, and hands them on more surely.
The Inherited Ground.fraying: Each new group of children takes on the adults' ways less fully, so the handed-down pattern fades.
The Inherited Ground.push: Change the ground early and for long: the loop is broken by a change of neighbourhood, or of a child's years in it ('younger children whose families moved to wealthier neighborhoods had an annual income 31 percent higher by their mid-twenties'). The Closed Circuit alone says act on any element; The Slow Hand alone says occupants enforce the setting's script. Only the pair says each cohort becomes the next cohort's setting, so the lever is how many childhood years are spent among which adults.

old_poles.tending: Children grow into the script the adults around them keep and grow up to be those adults for the next children, so a good arrangement is handed on without anyone teaching it.
old_poles.fraying: Each cohort grows up among the adults already living in a neighbourhood and becomes those adults for the next; disadvantage begets disadvantage.

pole_cases.tether: A street of readers raising children who become readers too.
pole_cases.snare: Hardship passing from parents to children on the same block.

The Priced Tradition.name: The Priced Tradition
The Priced Tradition.tending: Each family that keeps the custom adds to the price of dropping it, so the next family keeps it more surely.
The Priced Tradition.fraying: Each keeping family adds less to the price of dropping it, so the custom slips sooner for the next family.
The Priced Tradition.push: Do not ask one family to go first, and do not rely on changing what people are told. The conditions that pay for the practice are the other families' conduct, so words that change one mother's mind leave her to pay the whole price. Pay for the alternative for a large share of families at the same time, and give it the tradition's standing as a rite, so that when the payer withdraws, the families' own conduct holds it. Gneezy's FGM design 'purposefully targets a large fraction of girls in the community at the same time' and provides 'an alternate rite of passage'. It asks 'What's to stop a mother from circumcising her daughter at the conclusion of the four years?' and answers with the graduates' standing in the marriage market. The Held Commitment alone says to plan for the day the holder lets go, by adding a pledge of your own. Each Other's Situation alone says to change others by moving first yourself. Only the pair says that the held conditions are the others' conduct: a lone first mover is billed for the difference, and the paid alternative lasts only once enough families run it to become the condition. The Slow Hand's lever is to change the setting instead of the person; Critical Mass says to move a group together but not that the group must be paid and given the name.

old_poles.tending: Each family keeps the named practice because the other families' conduct pays for it, and by keeping it becomes part of what pays the next family. Where the practice named as the rite serves the families, the named role and its pay hold together without enforcement: the warriors who take the Scout post make it 'now the role of a warrior' for the next warriors, 'both making a decent living and preserving tradition' (Gneezy 419435), and conventions that 'coerce via expectations can be exceedingly helpful' (Schelling 219890).
old_poles.fraying: The named rite and what the others pay for it stay locked on a practice that harms the families. Mothers cut because grooms' families pay a larger dowry for a cut bride and peers shun the uncut; the grooms want a cut wife because they 'want her to be an accepted member of the community', and the community accepts the cut because most families cut. A mother whose mind is changed still faces conditions made of everyone else's conduct, so she alone pays for leaving ('that family then risks being ostracized by the community', Gneezy 428813). Social norms 'will tend to remain stable even when they help neither the group nor the individual' and resist 'efforts by one or a few individuals to change them' (Henrich 364189, 362395). Schelling makes the same point: 'people can be trapped into self-enforcing rules that misdirect behavior' (220026).

pole_cases.tether: Village festivals that keep crafts alive because skipping one draws scorn.
pole_cases.snare: Costly dowries kept by every family because the first to stop suffers.

The Covered Loss.name: The Covered Loss
The Covered Loss.tending: Losses get covered more fully and faster, so the covered side guards less and the covering side pays more.
The Covered Loss.fraying: Losses get covered less fully and slower, so the covered side guards more and the covering side pays less.
The Covered Loss.push: Relief that takes a loss off someone's account changes what they will do next, so price it against the care it removes. The Simba Project pays 70 percent, not 100, and less where the boma was neglected. That is a different move from Crowd-Out, where relief spends the pressure to change conditions, and from The Rescue, where relief confirms a story.

old_poles.tending: Relief moves a loss off the person who can least bear it, and with it goes the reason for a destructive response. Compensated for a cow a lion has taken, the elder no longer has to spear the lion himself.
old_poles.fraying: Once his loss is covered, the insured has less incentive to be careful and leaves the fence unmended, so the insurer ends up paying for the neglect its own cover made affordable. At scale, the finance firm takes wild risks and reaps wild profits, then lobbies for a bailout that leaves taxpayers to foot the bill.

pole_cases.tether: A herder paid for a lost cow, so the lion lives.
pole_cases.snare: A bank taking wild risks, sure a bailout will come.

The Clean Conscience.name: The Clean Conscience
The Clean Conscience.tending: The story takes in each cost faster and holds tighter, so the sense of fair play returns sooner each time.
The Clean Conscience.fraying: The story takes in each cost less, so the sense of fair play drifts and is slower to return.
The Clean Conscience.push: The story needs ambiguity to live in ('room for ambiguity or subjectivity in the recommendation'), so making the harm unambiguous and unrelabellable removes the self-deception without needing to change anyone's values. It differs from The Declared Interest, where the licence comes from a disclosure: here nothing is disclosed.

old_poles.tending: The self-story takes in what the account leaves out: acting to confirm 'I am someone who cares', a person carries a cost that shows on nobody's account, and the good they do falls on others unbilled. Sara hauls cans to the recycling center in the cold because the trip is a positive self-signal; 'she could have placed the cans in the trash'.
old_poles.fraying: Advice that favours the adviser is given in sincere belief that it was ethical. Queue-dodgers who lower other players' odds keep their self-image and their loot, and the pattern repeats because the story absorbs each repetition.

pole_cases.tether: A triage nurse making hard calls each shift without crushing guilt.
pole_cases.snare: An adviser pushing costly products while sure he's helping clients.

The Credited Result.name: The Credited Result
The Credited Result.tending: Credit pulls work harder toward what can be seen, so unseen work gets done less and less.
The Credited Result.fraying: Credit's pull on the work loosens, so more effort drifts back to work no one can see.
The Credited Result.push: Before trusting what a credit-seeker delivers, ask what the audience can actually see. Knowing that NL alone distorts the public's judgment and that the Outfall alone leaves costs off the account does not tell you that the two together steer a whole agenda toward the visible.

old_poles.tending: Where the valuable outcome is also the visible one, the public credits what it can see and the credit-seekers deliver what it credits, so seeking credit delivers the value.
old_poles.fraying: Programs whose results are invisible, such as childhood vaccination, go uncredited and underprovided. Tangible but hollow ones, such as neighbourhood beautification, get the credit.

pole_cases.tether: Fixing potholes everyone sees and everyone needs fixed.
pole_cases.snare: Schools teaching to the test while reading for pleasure fades.

The Unbroken Chain.name: The Unbroken Chain
The Unbroken Chain.tending: Each added day pulls harder toward the next, and the streak grips tighter the longer it grows.
The Unbroken Chain.fraying: Each added day pulls less toward the next, and the streak's grip loosens until missed days stop mattering.
The Unbroken Chain.push: Put the line on the attending itself, not on the result, and plan for the first break (never miss twice). The Line alone locates the zero-credit failure; this figure says which quantity to put the line on.

old_poles.tending: He shows up each day to add to his streak, and keeping the streak whole brings him back through bad and uninspired days: Seinfeld 'is not focused on how good or bad a particular joke is… He is simply focused on showing up and adding to his streak.'
old_poles.fraying: Once the chain breaks, he reads the broken streak as zero and stops attending: 'The first mistake is never the one that ruins you. It is the spiral of repeated mistakes that follows. … Missing twice is the start of a new habit.'

pole_cases.tether: A writer showing up daily through dry spells to finish a book.
pole_cases.snare: Someone running through an injury to keep a streak alive.

The Settled Expert.name: The Settled Expert
The Settled Expert.tending: Each win shapes the self-view more firmly, so the side holds tighter to whichever view it has, student or settled.
The Settled Expert.fraying: Each win shapes the self-view less, so how the side sees itself drifts more freely from what it has learned.
The Settled Expert.push: Treat your own success as the signal to recheck the gradient, not as the reading of it. Neither parent alone predicts that learning is what installs the story that ends it.

old_poles.tending: The runner keeps the story 'still a student' against the evidence of their own success, so each accomplishment points them to what they do not yet know and they go on seeking instruction.
old_poles.fraying: Accomplishment puffs up knowledge ('Scientia infla'), so the more the runner has learned, the more firmly they believe they are 'set and secure' in a field whose understanding is 'a fluid, continual process'. Arrogance 'puts blinders on' exactly where the learning still was.

pole_cases.tether: A veteran surgeon whose every success sends her back to study more.
pole_cases.snare: A star analyst so sure he stops checking his models.

The Shifted Burden.name: The Shifted Burden
The Shifted Burden.tending: Each time one side steps in, the other holds steady less on its own, so the gap comes back sooner and harder.
The Shifted Burden.fraying: Stepping in happens less, so the other side gets more practice holding steady and the gap returns slower.
The Shifted Burden.push: Judge the help by what the helped loop can still do on its own, not by the state it keeps. The better the intervenor holds the setpoint, the less the system's own balancing loop is exercised, so a well-held state is no evidence that the help is safe. Before withdrawing, rebuild that loop ('work in such a way as to restore or enhance the system's own ability to solve its problems, then remove yourself'); withdrawal alone leaves a system that can no longer find its setpoint. The Salve alone says relief atrophies the capacity it replaced; The Tide alone says a system returns toward its setpoint. Only the pair says the relief is standing in for the returning, so the capacity lost is the system's own ability to hold its state. It differs from Answering For (Salve + Salve), where both parties relieve themselves and the lever is the helper's urge; here the helped system has a setpoint of its own to recover.

old_poles.tending: The intervenor holds the state where it needs to be while the system's own loop is too weak to do it alone. Relief is taken on purpose and the setpoint is held better than the system could hold it (vaccination instead of partial natural immunity).
old_poles.fraying: Each relief hides the gap the system's own loop would have closed, so that loop does less. It weakens, the symptom comes back, more relief goes in, and in the end the system cannot hold its own state. Families can no longer care for their elderly, and farmers need fertiliser every season.

pole_cases.tether: Vaccines holding a town's health steadier than immunity alone could.
pole_cases.snare: Farmers needing more fertilizer every season as their soil weakens.

The Sure Voice.name: The Sure Voice
The Sure Voice.tending: Sounding sure wins more trust faster, so the other side sounds surer and surer each round.
The Sure Voice.fraying: Sounding sure wins less trust, so the other side leans on it less and doubt gets voiced more.
The Sure Voice.push: Neither party can break this alone: a client who is told to discount confidence still has nothing else to see, and an expert who admits uncertainty is replaced. Knowing the loop means grading experts on their track record rather than their manner, and building a place where admitting uncertainty is not punished.

old_poles.tending: Under dangerous uncertainty, a client's trust in a confident expert lets action happen where admitted guessing would paralyse it.
old_poles.fraying: Clients who cannot judge accuracy reward certainty. Experts who say how much they don't know are replaced by more confident rivals. The survivors explain away their failed predictions, and a clinician who is 'completely certain' is wrong 40% of the time.

pole_cases.tether: A crowd trusting a calm firefighter's sure orders during an evacuation.
pole_cases.snare: Patients rewarding a doctor who never admits what she doesn't know.

The Spent Margin.name: The Spent Margin
The Spent Margin.tending: Each added safety gets taken back faster as risk, so less of what it saved remains.
The Spent Margin.fraying: Added safety gets taken back as risk more slowly, so more of what it saved stays saved.
The Spent Margin.sources: CHATER; GNEEZY; Brownstein (weatherize, raise the thermostat)
The Spent Margin.push: Judge a safety arrangement by the outcome after the protected party has re-spent the margin, not by what the arrangement does on its own. Where compensation matters, shape what the person feels, not only the physics.

old_poles.tending: The protected party takes back part of the made-safer margin as freedom to act and still comes out ahead: people do take more risks once the protection is in, only less than the engineering gained.
old_poles.fraying: The protected party reads the protection as a sign that a crash, or an infection, will be survivable, and moves back toward the old level of risk. The helmetless passenger and the untreated partner carry the risk the protected party re-spent.

pole_cases.tether: Better brakes letting drivers reach home sooner, still safer overall.
pole_cases.snare: Drivers with antilock brakes tailgating until crashes climb back.

The Living Witness.name: The Living Witness
The Living Witness.tending: The witnesses' presence makes the telling seem surer each year, and the telling draws them back more firmly.
The Living Witness.fraying: The witnesses' presence lends the telling less weight each year, and fewer come back to stand behind it.
The Living Witness.push: Look at who is marching: while the event's own witnesses walk in the rite, a correction has to be made with them and inside the occasion, because correcting it from outside in print changes nothing. Plan for the witness generation's passing (Tannenwald's 'nuclear forgetting'), since that is when the telling either hardens into myth or loses its hold. Neither parent says this: Enacted Telling says argument cannot correct a telling fused to a rite; Standing Rite says whoever owns the occasion owns what is stored; only the composition names the witnesses as the certifying link.

old_poles.tending: While the people who lived the event still walk in its yearly occasion, they pass on the living memory of it themselves, and the telling stays tied to what they lived; the occasion can be kept without them only once no generation is still alive who can 'pass on the living memory'.
old_poles.fraying: The survivors march in the yearly rite while its owners, in the memorial address, retell the survivors' own event as its opposite (a fiasco as a sacrifice), and the survivors' marching is what certifies the retelling; the owners of the occasion rewrite the meaning while the witnesses supply the proof.

pole_cases.tether: Veterans keeping a memorial's story close to what they lived.
pole_cases.snare: Survivors' presence lending weight to a retelling that reverses their story.

The Rival Watch.name: The Rival Watch
The Rival Watch.tending: Each side watches the other's share more closely, so any overreach is caught sooner and pulled back harder.
The Rival Watch.fraying: Each side watches less closely, so overreach drifts further before anyone pulls it back.
The Rival Watch.push: Place the two parties who can harm each other face to face at the moment of harm (adjacent rotation turns, the next user waiting at the gate), so that the race supplies its own monitoring; where the harmed cannot see or call the harmer to account (strangers on a shared main, a neighbour hurt by an unofficial channel), no watch forms and an outside monitor is needed. Neither parent says where monitoring comes free: The Shared Pot says a two-sided commons can be bargained down, Mutual Monitoring says monitoring is a by-product of use, and only the composition says it is a by-product exactly where the race's two sides meet. It differs from The Contingent Commitment (Mutual Monitoring + Mutual Monitoring), which concerns how monitored information sustains contingent compliance, not where the monitors come from.

old_poles.tending: Users who can harm one another watch one another at no extra cost, because keeping one's own share means keeping an eye on the rival's; the next irrigator waiting at the gate holds the last one to his turn, and the family's watchers keep the hot water from being raced away.
old_poles.fraying: The same stake that makes every user a watcher makes every user a combatant: when everyone is watching everyone else over a scarce share, each suspected overrun is met by a user ready to fight for his water, and the watching carries a standing potential for violence among the rivals and against their agents.

pole_cases.tether: Neighboring farmers keeping each other to their turns at the gate.
pole_cases.snare: Roommates tracking every crumb until small slips turn into shouting matches.

The Limelight.name: The Limelight
The Limelight.tending: Each time the surest voice gets picked, it grows bolder and more famous, so it gets picked again faster.
The Limelight.fraying: Being picked brings less fame each time, so the surest voice grows bolder more slowly and gets picked less readily.
The Limelight.push: Do not buy calibration with more expertise or more fame. Past a low threshold both raise confidence faster than accuracy, so prefer a forecaster with a scored record who works away from the limelight. Neither parent says this: the Sure Voice push grades by track record but still assumes more knowledge helps, and the Settled Expert push is the expert's own recheck, which demand works against.

old_poles.tending: An expert whose learning has earned real conviction is sought out for it, and the clients who choose that confident voice get decisions made under dangerous uncertainty.
old_poles.fraying: Each gain in knowledge adds more to the expert's confidence than to his accuracy. Clients and producers choose the most confident voice. The choice brings fame, the famous expert forecasts more flamboyantly and explains his failures away, and the next choice goes to him again.

pole_cases.tether: A seasoned surgeon chosen for a risky case, steadying the room.
pole_cases.snare: A TV pundit's bold forecasts winning airtime despite many misses.

The Watched Promise.name: The Watched Promise
The Watched Promise.tending: Each kept word seen makes the next one surer, so both sides keep their word more and more tightly.
The Watched Promise.fraying: Each kept word seen counts for less, so slips come easier and each fine holds less sway.
The Watched Promise.push: Let the users harmed by an infraction find it and set the first sanction, and keep that sanction small. Whoever sets it is a rival who may be in the same situation next season, and a complier deciding from this case whether to keep complying. A small sanction tells him, and everyone who hears of it, that compliance is still high; a large one breeds the resentment he is watching for. Escalate only on repeat breach ('graduated sanctions initially for their informational value and eventually for their deterrence value'), and let users watch the guards as well as each other so that no single lapse cascades. The Contingent Commitment alone says keep the rules cheap to watch, because the watcher's compliance runs on what he sees. The Rival Watch alone says where monitoring comes free. Only the composition says that the free watcher also sets the sanction, so the size of the sanction is part of the information that sustains compliance (Ostrom's design principle 5). Of Ostrom's eight principles only 3-5 belong to this interlock. It differs from The Shared Pot (no watch), The Standoff (no monitoring), and Crowd-Out and The Priced Tradition (no watch leg).

old_poles.tending: Watching comes free and confirms that others comply, so compliance keeps itself going. The user-monitor who finds a lapse by someone who normally complies imposes 'only a modest sanction', since he 'might be in a similar situation in the future', and everyone who hears of it learns that compliance is still high. Where the watchers judge a wave of lapses temporary (Yamanaka in the Depression), they keep quiet out of 'confidence that the problem was temporary', and the commons holds.
old_poles.fraying: The watcher who sets the sanction is also a rival and a contingent complier. When he keeps finding a rival breaking the rules, he escalates 'the imposed sanctions in an effort to halt future rule-breaking by such offenders and any others who might start to follow suit'. A watcher who imposes a large fine on a user facing an unusual problem turns that user toward 'resentment and unwillingness to conform to the rules in the future', so the watcher's own escalation recruits the next breach.

pole_cases.tether: Fishers sharing a lake and keeping catch limits year after year.
pole_cases.snare: Neighbors so bound to watching each other that no one dares change.

Tipping.name: Tipping
Tipping.tending: Each exit leaves fewer of one kind behind, so the next ones leave sooner and the leaving speeds up.
Tipping.fraying: Each exit pushes fewer others to go, so the leaving slows and a mix lasts longer.
Tipping.push: Capping one side's numbers can create a stable mixture, and 'greater tolerance' does not always help. Limiting the number of whites works as if the excess had no tolerance: 'it is their absence that keeps the whites from overwhelming the blacks by their numbers' (Schelling 293946, 294556, 294685). Critical Mass alone says to get the activity past its minimum, so more entrants and more tolerance always help. Only the pairing shows that one run's success is what trips the other's thresholds, so quotas or limits on entry, not more tolerance, decide whether a mix holds.

old_poles.tending: Where the two tolerance schedules overlap widely, each colour's entry keeps the ratio inside the other's limits, so both keep entering and settle on a mixture that holds against fairly large disturbances: 'the dynamics of entry and departure will lead to the stable mixture of 80 blacks and 80 whites' (Schelling 292874, 293544).
old_poles.fraying: More of one colour move into a compatible mix, so the ratio passes the limits of the other colour's least tolerant members. Their exits lower the share of those of their colour who stay, the next ones leave, and the minority evacuates completely. The residents sort into an all-one-colour area even though a mix existed that both colours could accept (Schelling 291031, 291214).

pole_cases.tether: A bar's last smokers leaving as it turns smoke-free.
pole_cases.snare: A mixed block turning all one color within a decade.

The Counteroffer.name: The Counteroffer
The Counteroffer.tending: Each reply pulls the next offer closer to the last one, and the gap closes faster and holds.
The Counteroffer.fraying: Each reply pulls the next offer less toward the last one, so the numbers drift apart and stop meeting.
The Counteroffer.push: Your own counter is the other side's reference, so answering an outrageous number with an outrageous number locks the gap for both of you. Refuse the number instead of answering it (Kahneman: storm out, 'you will not continue the negotiation with that number on the table'; Voss: deflect or pivot to terms), or open high but reasonable so that reciprocal concessions can converge (Gneezy). The Tested Price alone says to test a named number before accepting it. It does not say that your reply feeds the other side's next reference.

old_poles.tending: Each offer is judged against the other's last one, so a concession by one is read as a gain and answered by a concession from the other; the gap narrows round by round to a number both can accept (Gneezy: 'I make a concession and then you make a concession', a give-and-take held to be 'fair').
old_poles.fraying: Each side answers the other's extreme number with an extreme number of its own, and each extreme becomes the other's reference, so both references move apart and fix a gap neither can bridge. The talks stall at impasse, or are dragged to a compromise set by whoever anchored hardest (Kahneman: 'a gap that will be difficult to bridge'; Voss: 'pulled into the compromise trap').

pole_cases.tether: Two traders quickly settling on a price both can live with.
pole_cases.snare: A seller conceding too fast after a lowball opening number.

The Leaking Border.name: The Leaking Border
The Leaking Border.tending: What one side saves flows over to the other faster and fuller, and the other side's take rises more quickly to match.
The Leaking Border.fraying: Less of what one side saves flows across, and the other's take rises slower, so each side keeps more of its saving.
The Leaking Border.push: Draw the watch around the resource, not around the group. A group whose own monitoring works should expect its savings to leak to an adjoining group that shares the resource and is still racing, and more watching inside its border only enlarges that subsidy; the move is to bring the neighbour into the same watch (a joint district, cross-border assurances such as a pledged curtailment to keep the flow coming, shared arenas). Neither run alone says this: one run of The Rival Watch says monitoring comes free among rivals inside a group, and The Shared Pot, the leg the two groups share, says rivals bill each other; only two interlocking runs say a group's successful watch makes it a better outfall for its neighbour. Distinct from The Watched Promise (watch-sustained compliance within one set of users).

old_poles.tending: Each group's watched restraint raises the shared water table for the other: a cutback and replenishment in Central Basin, where recharge works best, raise levels there and increase the flow into West Basin, so each group's kept promise pays into its neighbour's, and overlapping members carry word of what works across the border.
old_poles.fraying: The better one group's watch holds, the more of its saving flows to the neighbour still racing. West Basin's pumpers cut back under their agreement while Central Basin's pumpers, shielded by West Basin from the sea, draw down farther with no immediate cost and keep increasing withdrawals; the flow reverses toward the racers, and the conservers' restraint is spent subsidising the rival group's race.

pole_cases.tether: One town's water savings quickly refilling a drought-struck neighbor's wells.
pole_cases.snare: A country's emission cuts simply freeing room for a neighbor's factories.

The Long Line.name: The Long Line
The Long Line.tending: Each pick makes the next pick of the same choice easier, so the line grows faster.
The Long Line.fraying: Each pick adds less pull toward the same choice, so the line grows slower and other choices draw people.
The Long Line.push: When you choose between rivals, discount how many people are already choosing each one. That count is the first mover's prize, not a measurement. Judge the rival directly, or, where you run the choice, hide the count (the order of refusals, the length of the line). Seeding the cue works just as well to start a run on purpose (the barista's tip jar). First-Arriver Lock-In alone puts the fix on what the prize is made of. The Contagion alone says a form is caught and passed on. Only the pair says that the prize is other people's visible choosing, so the lever is whether that choosing is visible, not the judging and not the reward. Different from The Cascade (salience of one risk, not rivals ranked) and The Faithful Chain (what passes intact, not who gets copied).

old_poles.tending: Where earlier choosers really did see something, later choosers who join them carry their information forward. Learners use others' attention and deference to 'rapidly zero in on whom to learn from', and the skilled model gains the following that lets their know-how spread (Henrich).
old_poles.fraying: Choosers keep choosing whoever was chosen before, whether or not they deserve it. The model is followed 'even if they turn out not to be very knowledgeable or skilled', and a celebrity 'is born—seemingly from nothing' from one early exposure (Henrich). Customers queue at one cart and not at its identical twin across the street. A kidney refused by ninety-nine earlier patients is refused by the hundredth, and 'thousands of patients turn down kidneys they should have accepted' (Berger).

pole_cases.tether: Newcomers following crowds to the most skilled teacher in town.
pole_cases.snare: Patients refusing a kidney because many before them did.

The Firebreak.name: The Firebreak
The Firebreak.tending: Each case turned down makes the line harder, so the next near miss is argued less and dismissed faster.
The Firebreak.fraying: Each case turned down hardens the line less, so near misses keep being argued and the line blurs.
The Firebreak.push: When a bright line is being gamed by degree, refuse the exception on its category, not on its size or merits, even when the exception is defensible, because each one that passes shows the line has a price. This reverses Gaming the Terms' push (read evasion as feedback and revise the rule): for a named line, revising to fit the defensible case is the erosion. The Branded Line alone says a name holds a line and lets its outside pass. Gaming the Terms alone says tightening feeds evasion. Only the pair says that the evader's best cases must be refused, and that refusing them is what hardens the name. It differs from The Emerging Taboo, which concerns the window when reciprocity is all that holds the line, not evasion by degree.

old_poles.tending: Each attempt to fit a weapon or an explosion to the permitted side is argued out in the name, and each defeat hardens the line from argument toward the unarguable. The demise of 'peaceful nuclear explosions' and the political defeat of the neutron bomb 'contributed to the consolidation of the taboo'. By the end, a clean thermonuclear power scheme was 'unanimously dismissed without argument, as if the objections were too obvious to require articulation'.
old_poles.fraying: The rule-beaters keep producing weapons whose letter fits the permitted side. Very small, accurate 'mini-nukes' that could meet just-war criteria have 'already become a source of pressure on the norm', and each such weapon, if used, 'would erode the threshold, blur the firebreak, pave the way by incremental steps for nuclear escalation'.

pole_cases.tether: A ban on poison gas growing too firm to argue.
pole_cases.snare: A taboo so firm that a sound new idea is waved off.

It Was Allowed.name: It Was Allowed
It Was Allowed.tending: Each use of the gap feels more allowed, so the gap gets used more often and more boldly.
It Was Allowed.fraying: Each use feels a little less allowed, so the gap gets used less often and more carefully.
It Was Allowed.push: Where a rule's letter is the exploiter's alibi, do not argue with his conscience. Change the letter. Close the gap in the system, or rule on it explicitly as legitimate or as cheating, because what the system permits will be read as permission. The Clean Conscience alone says make the harm unrelabellable. Gaming the Terms alone says read the evasion as feedback. Only the pair says that the relabelling is supplied by the rule itself, so the fix belongs in the system, not in persuading the player.

old_poles.tending: A sincere reading of what the system allows finds play the designers never foresaw, and the community may ratify it: an apparent exploit 'might be embraced by the player community as a legitimate feature of the game' (Lemarchand). The exploiters 'see the places where the rules don't quite jibe' (Koster).
old_poles.fraying: The move lowers other players' odds, but it is allowed, so the players who make it 'saw themselves as good people who had sufficient reasons for technically breaking the rules' and repeat it as an ongoing pattern (Hopson). A stickler's correction reads to them as unfair (Koster), while everyone else resents 'circumvention'.

pole_cases.tether: Speedrunners turning a game glitch into a loved new sport.
pole_cases.snare: A firm repeating a tax loophole year after year, guilt-free.

The Shared Pot.name: The Shared Pot
The Shared Pot.tending: Each side's taking or care lands on the other harder, so the other takes or cares more, faster.
The Shared Pot.fraying: Each side's taking or care lands on the other less, so the other's answer grows weaker and slower.
The Shared Pot.status: book original; merged with the added figure The Pumping Race
The Shared Pot.push: When the ones harmed are themselves the runners, the cost appears on both accounts, so it can be claimed and traded against ('each producer had prescribed against all of the others'). A two-sided commons can therefore be bargained down by its own users in a way a one-way outfall cannot. Ostrom limits her self-governing cases to exactly this ('users can substantially harm one another').

former_book_entry.tending: A resource used freely because trust makes accounting unnecessary
former_book_entry.fraying: A resource nobody is positioned to protect

old_poles.tending: Because the parties are each other's outfall, each one's own-account act also leaves unbilled gifts for the others, and each one's act is worth more because the others act too: 'you benefit from the use of insecticides by others; the value of your own insecticides is dissipated unless some neighbors use insecticides, too.'
old_poles.fraying: Each side takes the benefit and bills a share of the cost to the other, whose taking bills it straight back: what one does not pump today a rival will, 'the two incentives reinforce one another', and the pool, pasture or road is run down by people who are each harming only one another.

pole_cases.tether: Farmers whose pest control grows more useful as neighbors join.
pole_cases.snare: Rival wells draining a shared water table faster every season.

Proxy Detachment.name: Proxy Detachment
Proxy Detachment.tending: Effort aims harder at where the number moves, so the number climbs faster and is called a win more surely.
Proxy Detachment.fraying: Effort aims less at the number, so it climbs slower and is called a win less often.
Proxy Detachment.status: book original; merged with the added figure The Captured Measure
Proxy Detachment.note: Carries the sincere cases (step counts, a number chased in good faith). Strategic cases, the per-mile contract and teacher incentive pay, belong to Gaming the Terms.
Proxy Detachment.push: Measure the thing nearer the purpose (customers who finish the meal, not revenue), treat every number as one piece of feedback, and change what you measure when the chase starts, because whoever attends to the number will optimise the number. The Gardener alone says attention grows what it touches; The Mark alone says you judge against a reference; only the pair says the reference is what attention grows. Gaming the Terms carries the strategic case.

former_book_entry.tending: A measure that makes a vast system legible
former_book_entry.fraying: A group works obediently toward an indicator that was defined incompletely, and produces a result nobody intended while the indicator reads as success.

old_poles.tending: Runners who share one reference aim their attention at the same thing, and while they use the number as a guide within a larger picture, their attention grows what it stands for.
old_poles.fraying: Attention attaches to the proxy; the runners chase the number and report success while the thing withers.

pole_cases.tether: A clinic driving down wait times as patients do get seen faster.
pole_cases.snare: Schools raising test scores by drilling the test while reading slips.

The Slow Hand.name: The Slow Hand
The Slow Hand.tending: The people in the place hold each other to the easiest way more tightly, so the setup stays fixed more firmly.
The Slow Hand.fraying: The people hold each other to the easiest way more loosely, so other ways of acting spread and the setup shifts.
The Slow Hand.status: book original; merged with the added figure The Standing Script
The Slow Hand.push: When someone keeps failing to fit, look at the setting's script and at the occupants enforcing it before reading the failure as character, and change the setting rather than the person (Duckworth: 'we must train our eye on the place, not the person'). Choice Architecture alone says the arranger makes one option nearest, Each Other's Situation alone says people make each other's conditions; only the pair says the occupants enforce the arranger's script, so its effects are misread as their own traits.

former_book_entry.tending: Continuity outlasting any single life's turbulence
former_book_entry.fraying: An early arrangement enforcing itself long after anyone chose it, defended by the interests it created, so changing it means beating them first.

old_poles.tending: Whoever arranged the setting made the right move nearest, and the occupants hold each other to it.
old_poles.fraying: The occupants enforce the setting's script on whoever does not fit it, and its effects are read as their character.

pole_cases.tether: A quiet library where everyone keeps everyone else hushed.
pole_cases.snare: A school blaming one restless child instead of the cramped room.

Transmission Drift.name: Transmission Drift
Transmission Drift.tending: Each telling shifts the memory more, and the shifted version is told faster and held more surely.
Transmission Drift.fraying: Each telling shifts the memory less, so the story moves more slowly away from what happened.
Transmission Drift.status: book original; merged with the added figure The Told Self
Transmission Drift.note: poles first written in the registry pass; previously held only in conversation
Transmission Drift.push: Check a retold memory against a recording made at the time, and trust confidence least in the stories told most often, since with retelling 'accuracy declined, but confidence remained high'. The Keepsake alone says an episode is stored by its peak and close; the Namer alone says words build what follows. Only the pair says each telling rewrites the stored episode, so the only fixed check is one made outside the telling ('Recordings are snapshots in time').

former_book_entry.tending: A story that survives by adapting to each teller
former_book_entry.fraying: A story drifted free of what it started as

old_poles.tending: Each retelling ties the stored episode to the teller's present self, so a told memory becomes a touchstone for who the teller has been ('True or not, this memory is a touchstone for my past-self'), and the tellings together keep an identity continuous.
old_poles.fraying: Inaccurate memories repeated rather than corrected, further ingrained

pole_cases.tether: A family tale growing into a story that binds the generations.
pole_cases.snare: A witness's retold account shifting further from what was seen.

The Endorsement.name: The Endorsement
The Endorsement.tending: Each copy draws more eyes to the famous one, so more habits get copied, faster and further from its skill.
The Endorsement.fraying: Each copy draws fewer eyes, so fame cools and fewer of the famous one's habits get copied.
The Endorsement.push: Before you copy a prestigious person's habit, advice or choice, ask two things. Does the success they are known for bear on this domain? And did their prestige come from skill, or only from attention? From the sender's side, the carrier of a practice can be picked for prestige rather than for expertise, and Henrich calls this 'a powerful and underutilized public health tool'. The Long Line alone says to discount the count of choosers. The Faithful Chain alone says to strip the irrelevant steps before a prestigious model demonstrates. Only the pair says that the queue's prize is a licence to be copied everywhere, so the lever is the domain of the copying, not the count and not the procedure.

old_poles.tending: Learners copy a prestigious model broadly because they cannot yet tell which of the model's habits carry the success. When the model's conduct is sound, the practice reaches people whom slow campaigns do not reach. One celebrity's account of a preventive decision 'flooded clinics from the U.K. to New Zealand with women seeking genetic screenings' (Henrich).
old_poles.fraying: Prestige that attention conferred is copied in domains where the model has no competence. A basketball star is paid to recommend insurance, and a golfer's word moves opinions on car quality. When a celebrity dies by suicide, learners who resemble the celebrity copy the act and its method, and the result is extra suicides, 'not tragedies that would have occurred anyway' (Henrich). Each copy adds to the attention that keeps the model worth copying.

pole_cases.tether: A star's cancer screening sending thousands to get checked.
pole_cases.snare: A sports star's word selling shaky insurance to fans.

The Shared Alibi.name: The Shared Alibi
The Shared Alibi.tending: Each move that bends the rules pulls the other along faster, and each points to the other more surely.
The Shared Alibi.fraying: Each bending move pulls the other along less, and pointing to the other carries less weight as an excuse.
The Shared Alibi.push: Where an exploit is done in groups, sanction the repeated pattern, not the first try (Hopson banned only 'an ongoing pattern'). Break the coupling as well, so that one player's move does not force the others' hand, because the forced second move is what supplies the alibi. One run of It Was Allowed says to change the letter, because the rule is the exploiter's alibi. Only two interlocking runs say that the alibi is supplied by the other exploiters, so the lever is the link between players, and a first offence is not the thing to punish.

old_poles.tending: Players who take up a permitted move together, each reading it as allowed because the others read it so, carry it until the community ratifies it as legitimate play.
old_poles.fraying: Once one player dodges, the teammates face a loss if they stay, and the peer pressure 'helped a lot of players go along with something they might not have done if they were playing alone'. Each one then cites the others: banned players were far more likely than others to agree that people 'cannot be blamed for doing things that are technically wrong when all their friends are doing it too' (20% against 8%). The excuse that was true once is reused, and the dodge becomes an ongoing pattern across the whole team (Hopson).

pole_cases.tether: Players together turning a clever trick into accepted fair play.
pole_cases.snare: A team spreading a cheat because everyone else is doing it.

The Revolving Door.name: The Revolving Door
The Revolving Door.tending: Gifts bring easier rulings faster, and each ruling brings bigger gifts sooner, so the trade between the two speeds up.
The Revolving Door.fraying: Gifts win fewer easy rulings, and rulings bring smaller gains, so the trade between the two slows.
The Revolving Door.push: Do not treat capture as bad character to be exposed one case at a time, and do not count only on organising the diffuse side. Cut the channel through which the regulated shape the regulator's own conditions: cooling-off rules on the revolving door, gift and donation limits, and appointments that are not owed to the regulated. Apply these hardest at the top, where the rules 'are often weakest where they matter the most'. Chater calls the FDA revolving door 'largely unregulated (but easily fixed with an s-frame policy change)'. The Organized Few alone says the diffuse many do not resist, so it points to concentrating the many. The Arrangement alone says two parties shape each other's conditions. Only the pair says the rule-shaping travels through the rule-holder's own conditions, so the lever is what the rule-holder is paid in. This differs from The Two Hands (the personal fix spends the many's pressure) and from First-Arriver Lock-In (a reinvested prize, not a bought ruling).

old_poles.tending: The rule-holders and the interests they regulate each shape the other's conditions. Where the interests' gain runs with the public's, the rules they help write make the productive act the easy one for both sides.
old_poles.fraying: The few shape the regulators' and politicians' conditions with gifts, donations, support and future jobs. The regulators and politicians shape the few's conditions with rulings, protections and spoils. So the rules go to whoever is inside the alliance, and the cost falls on everyone outside it. Purdue 'managed to effectively infiltrate the Food and Drug Administration to obtain rulings favorable to their business', and its reviewers then took jobs at Purdue. At Kirindi Oya, large landowners captured the Cultivation Committees and bought protection for water theft through political contacts. Over time the alliance leaves 'a very small percentage of the population gaining and controlling exceptionally large percentages of the total wealth and power' (Dalio).

pole_cases.tether: Solar makers and lawmakers trading favors that make clean power cheap.
pole_cases.snare: A drug maker winning soft rulings by hiring its own reviewers.

The Largest Taker.name: The Largest Taker
The Largest Taker.tending: The biggest taker bends the rules harder, the others grab faster, and the pool drains quicker each round.
The Largest Taker.fraying: The biggest taker bends the rules less, the others grab less hard, and the pool drains slower.
The Largest Taker.push: In a race over a shared pool, find the largest taker first. It will carry the cost of restraint only while its share of the gain covers the free riding it feeds: by the 1930s Pasadena 'was no longer willing to undertake independent actions that were substantially benefiting others who were not contributing to the costs', took the whole race to court, and the parties 'then shared a single, authoritative image of the problem they faced'. So bring it into a rule that binds every taker (Pasadena's suit, a referee's single count of the safe yield) before it tires. Where the largest takers have instead captured the rule-making, organise the rest around them, not through them: at Gal Oya the organisations were 'nonpartisan' and bypassed 'those who had been the elite'. The Shared Pot alone says each taker bills the others. The Organized Few alone says the few shape rules the diffuse many do not resist. Only the pair says the many do not stay still. They race, so whether the largest taker spends its weight on the pool or on its own taking sets the race's direction. This differs from The Rival Watch, where the watching itself becomes the fight.

old_poles.tending: The largest taker spends its weight on the pool: its stake is large enough that it pays for what the race cannot, and the other takers draw on what it pays for. Pasadena 'replenished the basin by capturing floodwaters', and 'the water that percolated into the basin was then available for capture by the city of Pasadena as well as by other groundwater producers'.
old_poles.fraying: The largest takers spend their weight on their own taking instead: they shape the rules around it. At Kirindi Oya they captured the Cultivation Committees and 'obtained special privileges related to water distribution through internal influence or by seeking external political intervention'. The other appropriators, seeing that the rule does not hold for the strong, race harder: 'the only reasonable strategy to follow in a system in which others steal water with impunity ... is to flood their own fields as much as possible'. The pool runs down faster than a plain race would run it.

pole_cases.tether: A rigged quota system collapsing fast, forcing new rules sooner.
pole_cases.snare: Irrigators flooding their fields once officials take extra water.

The Insider's Objection.name: The Insider's Objection
The Insider's Objection.tending: The stake makes reasons against each rule sound fairer, so each new try is pushed back harder and faster.
The Insider's Objection.fraying: The stake colors the reasons less, so the push against each new try loosens and fades.
The Insider's Objection.push: Do not judge a rule by how reasonable its targets find the objections. Test the objections on the same rule aimed at another group: the doctors and the Times readers 'had similarly positive views on the policies aimed at avoiding conflicts of interest among financial planners', and parted only on the rule aimed at doctors. The Clean Conscience alone says the story needs ambiguity, so it points to making the harm unambiguous. The Organized Few alone says concentrate the diffuse side. Only the pair says the group's rule-shaping is sincere, so persuading its members will not work. The test is to swap the target.

old_poles.tending: Where a rule really would harm the group's work, the members' confidence in their own reasons makes them its most informed and energetic opponents.
old_poles.fraying: The group that a rule would bind finds every argument against it reasonable, and sincerely so. The physicians 'hated the policy proposals aimed at avoiding conflicts of interests for doctors' and 'rated every objection to the policy as more reasonable than did the Times readers', yet backed the same policy for financial planners. Because each member believes the incentive does not move him, the group opposes the rule without feeling self-interested. The conflict stays, and the next reform meets 'substantial opposition ... from those ... who benefit'.

pole_cases.tether: Doctors pushing back on a rule that would block needed care.
pole_cases.snare: Doctors fighting conflict-of-interest rules they'd back for anyone else.

The Untouched Judgment.name: The Untouched Judgment
The Untouched Judgment.tending: More gifts are taken with more certainty that judgment stays untouched, so limits get fought harder.
The Untouched Judgment.fraying: Gifts land with less certainty that judgment stays untouched, so limits get fought less and some take hold.
The Untouched Judgment.push: Take the decision on the curb away from the people it would bind: have it set and enforced for the top by a body outside the network, and write it as a bright line that holds whatever the official believes (fixed cooling-off periods, gift bans), not as self-assessed recusal or case-by-case conflict review. The senior figures it would bind are 'especially well-placed to block such oversight— and incentivized to do so', and they block it sincerely: 'All parties can deny that their judgment is corrupted ... (and some may believe this to be true)'. The Revolving Door alone says what to cut: the channel, hardest at the top. The Insider's Objection alone says test the objections by swapping the target. Only the pair says why the cut stays weakest at the top: the people it would bind are the ones who approve it, and they block it in good faith. So this figure's lever is who decides on the cut ('exposing and breaking up these networks' from outside them), not what the cut is or how well it is argued.
The Untouched Judgment.note: Push wording ('a body outside the network') is the catalogue's; Chater says the most senior block oversight and that networks of influence should be exposed and broken up.

old_poles.tending: People who move between the regulator and the regulated carry knowledge both ways. Because each trusts his own judgment, the network argues its case openly. Where its gain runs with the public's, the insiders' confident opposition keeps out rules that would cost everyone.
old_poles.fraying: Firms and donors shape officials' and judges' conditions with gifts, trips, donations and the job after office. The officials take them, and believing their own decisions 'unbiased and unaffected by the incentives they face', they meet each proposed curb as an unreasonable attack. The most senior, who hold the most favours, are 'especially well-placed to block such oversight— and incentivized to do so'. So the curbs stay weakest at the top, the channel stays open, and each new favour lands on a judgment that still feels untouched.

pole_cases.tether: Insiders blocking a costly rule that would hurt everyone.
pole_cases.snare: A judge on donor-paid trips blocking every ethics rule.

The Fuelled Spiral.name: The Fuelled Spiral
The Fuelled Spiral.tending: The slide feeds itself faster, and each round of relief joins the run more strongly, wherever it is aimed.
The Fuelled Spiral.fraying: The slide feeds itself less, and each round of relief joins the run more weakly, so it slows.
The Fuelled Spiral.note: Seated 2026-09-24 in the empty-link sweep for the Weaving wheel; reviewed blind.
The Fuelled Spiral.push: Where the relief flows decides which spiral it feeds: the same relief can stop a self-reinforcing run or become its next input, so judge relief by what it feeds, not by the symptom it eases, and dose it against the spiral's own rate. The Salve alone says relief leaves the cause in place and costs more each time, and The Spark alone says output feeds input; only the pair says the relief can itself be a spiral's fuel.

old_poles.tending: Relief is reached for against a run feeding on itself and goes where the compounding is productive: printed money and debt relief flow into production and profits, and the upswing that follows eases the pressure that called for relief, in a dose that offsets the downward spiral without starting the inflationary one.
old_poles.fraying: Each relief (printing to hold rates down) becomes an input to the spiral it answers (holders flee the devalued money), the spiral's next turn brings more pressure, and relief is reached for again, until the run 'can't be stopped'.

pole_cases.tether: Stimulus spending turning a slump into a fast-growing recovery.
pole_cases.snare: Printing money to fix inflation and sending prices higher still.

The New Normal.name: The New Normal
The New Normal.tending: What is in place becomes the usual faster, and each change is judged against it more firmly, so it is kept more surely.
The New Normal.fraying: What is in place settles in slower and holds less firmly, so changes are judged against it less and come easier.
The New Normal.note: Seated 2026-09-24 in the empty-link sweep for the Weaving wheel; reviewed blind.
The New Normal.push: Do not decide whether to change an arrangement by polling judgment of it before it exists: the arrangement in place sets the reference that will judge it, so trial it (Stockholm) and let the reference move; and read opposition to an existing arrangement's removal as partly an artifact of it being the reference, not proof of its worth. Neither 'people judge against a reference' nor 'shape conditions so the good action is easy' says that the shaped conditions become the reference.

old_poles.tending: A rule that makes the better action easiest, once in place, becomes the baseline people judge from, so it gains the support that keeps it and makes room for the next step.
old_poles.fraying: Whatever arrangement is already in place, however bad or captured, is the baseline every proposed change is judged against, so change registers as loss and the arrangement stays; anticipating that judgment, those who shape conditions stop proposing the next arrangement at all.

pole_cases.tether: A new seatbelt law soon feeling like how things have always been.
pole_cases.snare: An outdated tax rule kept because any fix feels like loss.
